title: A Summer to Remember: Recapping the 2026 JOOLA Pops Summer Tour
dek: Author: Corey Bockhaus This summer, JOOLA did something it had never done before: it put the whole brand on wheels. The 2026 JOOLA Pops Summer Tour brought the JOOLA Pops Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Author: Corey Bockhaus

This summer, JOOLA did something it had never done before: it put the whole brand on wheels. The 2026 JOOLA Pops Summer Tour brought the JOOLA Pops ice cream truck across the country, turning courts and community events into full-blown summer parties — complete with Rally Rocket paddle demos, carnival-style games, giveaways, and (of course) free popsicles.  

It was JOOLA’s first-ever tour of its kind, built to surprise and delight players wherever they found them, and to put the brand in front of new audiences who may have never picked up a paddle before. By the time the truck rolled its last mile, the tour had racked up 34 activations across 15 cities, drawn 4,700+ attendees, handed out 3,147 complimentary popsicles, and put paddles in hands for 400+ demos. From the first stop in Dallas to the last one on the East Coast, the tour was proof that summer really is better with a JOOLA in your hand.

Tour Stops

Dallas, TX kicked things off at Pickler Universe, tying in with the Dallas MLP event and giving fans their first-ever look (and taste) of the Rally Rocket collection.

From there, the tour pushed into Arkansas and Tennessee, bringing the same sun-soaked energy to communities that don’t always get the big brand activations — proving the JOOLA Summer wasn’t just for major markets.

St. Louis, MO brought the Midwest into the mix with a three-stop stretch: the Dwight Davis Tennis Center, followed by back-to-back visits to the Missouri Pickleball Club locations in Fenton and Ellisville, with lines forming early for popsicles and paddle demos at every stop.

Chicago, IL turned up the volume even more at SPF Chicago, with the truck parked in the middle of the city’s thriving pickleball scene.

The tour kept rolling through Indiana, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, where nostalgia was the name of the game — the drippy, red-white-and-blue Rally Rocket design and classic popsicle-truck vibe had players of every generation feeling like kids again.

By the time the truck hit New York City, the energy had reached a fever pitch, with back-to-back stops at CityPickle Atlantic Terminal and CityPickle Hudson Yards, where fans lined up for a chance to demo the Pro V Rally Rocket paddles before they even officially launched.

New Jersey kept the momentum going before the tour turned toward the DMV, where it stacked several stops in quick succession: Club Volo in Baltimore, Copper Union, the YMCA in Silver Spring, and Washington, D.C. in between.

The tour wrapped its final stretch with Delaware and a stop at Pickleball Virginia Beach — fitting, since the JOOLA Pops Summer Tour was dreamed up right in JOOLA’s own backyard of North Bethesda, MD. These final stops brought the tour full circle, closing out the summer with the same fun-first energy it started with.

Talk of the Town

Across every stop, one thing was clear: people couldn’t stop talking about the JOOLA Pops Summer Tour. On TikTok, creators leaned all the way into the nostalgia, framing the Rally Rocket collection as a paddle that “looks like a snack” and “plays like a dream,” with unboxing videos calling out the popsicle-inspired packaging, stickers, and ice-like accessories that came with it. 

The energy carried over to Instagram, where accounts like PROSHOT Pickleball shared reel coverage of the truck’s stops as they happened.

Pickleball media picked up on the same enthusiasm. Empower Pickleball framed the tour as a genuine culture moment rather than typical gear marketing, tapping into the nostalgia and community feel that drew a lot of players to the sport in the first place. The Dink Pickleball covered the tour’s city-by-city itinerary and the ice cream truck centerpiece as the tour kicked off.

A Summer of Memories

The 2026 JOOLA Pops Summer Tour was more than a launch for the Rally Rocket paddle (*limited number of paddles available until July 31 on JOOLA.com)— it was a celebration of everything summer and pickleball have in common: joy, nostalgia, and a reason to get outside and play. From Dallas to Delaware, the tour turned ordinary courts and community spaces into pop-up parties, introduced new players to the game, and gave longtime fans a summer they won’t forget.

By the numbers, it was a summer for the books:

  • 34 activations across 15 cities
  • 4,700+ attendees
  • 3,147 complimentary popsicles distributed
  • 400+ paddle demos conducted

It was the first tour of its kind for JOOLA, and if the numbers — and the reaction from every stop — are any indication, it won’t be the last.

Relive the whole summer — every stop, every popsicle, every rally — in the album below.

title: Pickleball Inc. and Pickleball World Cup Unite to Expand Global Competition and Open the Door for PPA Professionals to Represent Their Countries
dek: Pickleball Inc., the world’s largest professional and amateur pickleball ecosystem, and the Pickleball World Cup today announced a landmark strategic partnership designed to accelerate the global growth of pickleball through Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
Pickleball Inc., the world’s largest professional and amateur pickleball ecosystem, and the Pickleball World Cup today announced a landmark strategic partnership designed to accelerate the global growth of pickleball through expanded international competition, commercial collaboration, and worldwide media distribution.

Pickleball Inc. will serve as the exclusive media rights and commercial sponsorship partner for the Pickleball World Cup while also collaborating on broadcast distribution, international marketing, strategic partnerships, business development, and fan engagement initiatives to elevate one of the sport’s premier international competitions. The collaboration represents a shared vision between both organizations that pickleball’s future will be built not only through professional tours, but through continued investment in meaningful international competition.

Founded by Peruvian siblings, Hercilio Cabieses and Miranda Cabieses, the Pickleball World Cup has rapidly become a showcase for international competition, bringing together athletes from around the world to compete under their national flags. One of the most significant components of the partnership is that Pickleball Inc. has lifted its previous restriction on PPA Tour player participation in the Pickleball World Cup, allowing eligible professionals to represent their home countries beginning at the 2027 edition.

“We are incredibly excited to partner with Pickleball Inc. and unlock the tremendous opportunities this relationship will create. We started this journey with the goal to see pickleball in the Olympics, and with the expertise and resources of Pickleball Inc. we are a step closer,” said Hercilio Cabieses, Founder and CEO of the Pickleball World Cup. “Their experience and leadership in professional pickleball, media, and commercial partnerships will help elevate every aspect of the event, and will allow the world’s best players to join us in creating an unforgettable experience for athletes, fans, and federations alike.”

“The Pickleball World Cup embodies everything that makes international sports so compelling: national pride, elite competition, and the ability to unite people through sport,” said Connor Pardoe, CEO of Pickleball Inc. “Hercilio, Miranda and their team have built something truly special, and we are excited to help expand its global reach while creating new opportunities for players and fans around the world.”

The partnership with the Pickleball World Cup is another marquee moment for Pickleball Inc. and the international strategy of the PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball. The last few years have seen the genesis of PPA Asia, PPA Australia, PPA Canada, PPA Italy and PPA Spain, with more international opportunities on the horizon. Currently, PPA Tour athletes in the Top 20 across disciplines (singles, doubles and mixed doubles) represent 18 different countries.

“This is one of many important steps toward establishing pickleball as a truly global sport,” said Chris Patrick,  President of International at Pickleball Inc. “For our PPA professionals, this continues to open new ground, the chance to represent their country on an international stage, build their profile with new fan bases, and grow their earning potential beyond the domestic tour. It’s the kind of global opportunity our athletes have been asking for, and it’s a meaningful step as we continue building toward the future and pursuing our Olympic aspirations.”

As pickleball continues to unite professional and amateur players from nations around the world, this moment represents far more than a partnership, it is a historic and defining milestone in the sport’s evolution and a significant step toward shaping its future on the global stage.

title: PARTNERS Nominated for “Best Episodic Series” at Tribeca X
dek: PARTNERS, the highly successful docuseries from Carvana, Shutterstock Studios, and the Carvana PPA Tour, has been nominated for “Best Episodic Series” at Tribeca X, the Tribeca Film Festival’s flagship program Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
PARTNERS, the highly successful docuseries from Carvana, Shutterstock Studios, and the Carvana PPA Tour, has been nominated for “Best Episodic Series” at Tribeca X, the Tribeca Film Festival’s flagship program dedicated to brand-supported storytelling. 

Consisting of six separate episodes, PARTNERS provides an intimate look at the flourishing world of professional pickleball. Showcasing America’s fastest growing sport from the courts to the boardrooms, the PARTNERS cameras captured the thrills, spills, and tea of the biggest stars of the Carvana PPA Tour. The series features prominent figures such as Carvana PPA Tour Founder and CEO Connor Pardoe, whose vision and leadership has had an unmatched influence on the sport’s landscape, as well as star players such as Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns, the most decorated female and male players in pickleball history. Their stories, along with those of other athletes, highlight the dedication and passion driving the sport’s meteoric rise.

Since its release on May 6, 2026, PARTNERS has seen millions of views across platforms and has been praised for its authentic storytelling and in-depth exploration of the professional pickleball world. With unprecedented access on and off the court, PARTNERS captures the ambition, intensity, and personal drama behind the fastest-growing sport in America.

This Tribeca X nomination places PARTNERS alongside the top brand-supported content recognized for excellence in storytelling. This acknowledgment reflects the series’ success in engaging audiences and elevating the profile of professional pickleball on a global stage. 
PARTNERS is available to stream for free on the Carvana PPA Tour’s YouTube channel, Pickleballtv, and Prime Video.

title: Professional Pickleball Association Announces PPA Spain – Newest International Expansion of Global Leader in Pro and Amateur Pickleball
dek: The Professional Pickleball Association, the global leader in pro and amateur pickleball, is thrilled to announce further international expansion with a seven-tournament tour in Spain. The inaugural PPA Spain season Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
The Professional Pickleball Association, the global leader in pro and amateur pickleball, is thrilled to announce further international expansion with a seven-tournament tour in Spain. The inaugural PPA Spain season will begin Sept. 23-27 in Barcelona, with the remaining six tournaments spanning the country. PPA Spain will feature two PPA125 point-level tournaments, three PPA250s, and two marquee PPA500s. All points ladder up into one global PPA Tour ranking system, providing a clear pathway to becoming the best in the world.

“Pickleball is growing exponentially internationally, and we want to bring the absolute best of the sport to in-demand markets,” said Chris Patrick, President, International, Carvana PPA Tour. “Spain has shown a great appetite for pickleball and the elite level of pickleball that PPA Spain will showcase will help accelerate the sport’s growth in the region. Through professional and amateur competitions, PPA Spain will increase awareness of the sport by promoting the sportsmanship, fun, and social good that pickleball brings to communities.”

The seven-tournament slate is as follows:

Competition Divisions Available (across Men’s Singles, Men’s Doubles, Women’s Singles, Women’s Doubles and Mixed Doubles):

  • Age 19+ – Pro / 4.5 / 3.5 
  • Age 50+ – 4.5 / 3.5 
  • Age 60+ – 4.5 / 3.5 
  • Junior (16-18 years) – 5.0 / 4.5

More information on registering to compete at these events is coming soon. 

“Bringing the PPA Tour to Spain is a monumental milestone for the development of pickleball not just locally, but across all of Europe,” said Albert Escofet, CEO and Founder of Smash Pickleball Agency. “This will act as a massive catalyst, driving unprecedented growth in both player participation and the surrounding industry. Our ultimate vision is to propel pickleball onto the global stage, reaching metrics and a level of cultural importance comparable to traditional giant sports.”

America’s fastest growing sport is finding new ground internationally and Spain is primed to foster an explosion of pickleball popularity across the Iberian Peninsula. With the strength of the PPA behind it, PPA Spain will become a launching pad for Spain’s best players to continue their journey to the top ranks of professional pickleball, as they grow the game and promote pickleball to new and eager audiences. 

PPA Spain joins Asia, Australia, Canada and Italy as international professional pickleball tours governed and overseen by the Carvana PPA Tour, the global leader in professional and amateur pickleball.

title: *ABC’s of the 2025-2026 PPA Tour Season (*Anna Leigh and Ben’s Championships)
dek: (Stats cited refer to gold medal matches) ANNA LEIGH WATERS: BEN JOHNS: Johns is the only player to have won at least one gold medal in every year since the Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
(Stats cited refer to gold medal matches)

ANNA LEIGH WATERS:

  • Medals: Waters won medals in all 46 of the events she played in. 43 gold medals, one silver, and two bronzes. 
  • Singles: Waters won 12 times in 12 tournaments, running her streak to 25 tournaments in which she entered. In those 12 gold medal matches, Waters won 24 games while losing only one game, to Kate Fahey in Utah. Waters had more “Clean Winners” then her opponent in eleven of those twelve matches.
  • Doubles: Waters won 16 gold medals and two bronzes in 18 tournaments. Waters finished 2025 with a title at Daytona Beach with Jorja Johnson. Waters and Anna Bright, in their 15 finals together, lost only two games, both to Tyra Black and Parris Todd. They had more “Clean Winners” than their opponents in 13 of those 15 finals. Bright and Waters finished the season with seven straight three-game sweeps. 
  • Mixed Doubles: Waters and Ben Johns won 15 gold medals and one silver in 16 tournaments. Their silver was to Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin in three games at Mesa. Bright and Patriquin forced them to a four-game final twice and a five-game final twice. The Johnsons also pushed Waters and Johns to a five-game final. Waters and Johns finished their season with three three-game sweeps.
  • Triple Crowns: Waters played in all three disciplines 12 times and earned Triple Crowns in ten of them, raising her PPA Tour-record total to 44. She has won Triple Crowns in at least three consecutive tournaments six different times.
  • Greatness on Gold Medal Games: Waters won 85% of the games played in gold medal matches, compiling a record of 96-16. She or her team won in the minimum number of games necessary in 34 of those 44 gold medal matches.
  • 2026-2027: Waters enters the 2026-2027 season with 194 titles: 63 Singles, 65 Doubles, and 66 Mixed Doubles. Her “lowest” total, 63 in Singles, is still more than the overall career titles won by any other player other than Ben Johns. Her longest active winning streak in tournaments entered is 25 in Singles, dating back to May 2024.

BEN JOHNS: 

  • Medals: Johns won 31 gold medals and two silvers. He won golds in both Men’s Doubles and Mixed Doubles at a tournament 14 times.
  • Singles: For the first year or season in his career, Ben did not win a Singles title. He won a silver at Mesa, losing to Chris Haworth in the final. He lost in earlier rounds five times, and did not play Singles, or did not play at all, in the other 14 tournaments. 
  • Doubles: Johns and Gabe Tardio won 16 of the 17 tournaments they entered, getting knocked off the medal podium only once, at the World Championships. Nine of their 16 gold medal matches were three-game sweeps. Christian Alshon played this team especially tough. He was an opponent in five of the seven finals that went more than three games. Hayden Patriquin was in four of those four- or five-game finals. Johns and Tardio finished the season by winning eight consecutive tournaments, a record in Men’s Doubles.
  • Mixed: Johns and Waters won 15 golds and one silver together. They won ten tournaments together before losing in Mesa, then they won the last five tournaments they entered.
  • Triple Crowns: Johns did not have a Triple Crown this season. He played in all three finals only once, at Mesa. He has 21 career Triple Crowns.
  • Greatness on Gold Medal Games: Johns won 81% of the games he played in gold medal matches, compiling a record of 64-15.  Johns or his team won in the minimum number of games necessary in 18 of those 33 gold medal matches.
  • 2026-2027: Johns enters the new season with 185 titles: 42 Singles, 64 Doubles, and 79 Mixed Doubles. His “lowest” total, 42 in Singles, is still more than the overall career titles won by any other player other than Waters and Catherine Parenteau. His longest active winning streak in tournaments entered is ten in Doubles, starting in Lakeland last November.  

Johns is the only player to have won at least one gold medal in every year since the Tour’s inception in 2020. This Fall he is expected to win a gold medal in his 100th different tournament.

title: The Defense Does NOT Rest for Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters
dek: One of the things that makes Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters so tough to beat is their world-class defense. This is primarily evident from their scores. For example, they Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
One of the things that makes Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters so tough to beat is their world-class defense. This is primarily evident from their scores. For example, they swept their last five gold medal matches, winning each game by an average score of 11 – 3.33.

Another stat that sheds light on the caliber of defense is “Clean Winners” allowed. A “Clean Winner” is a rally-ending shot, safely “in,” that does not hit the net cord or an opponent’s paddle. Bright and Waters are excellent at getting shots back over the net, or at least getting a paddle on them, denying their opponents the satisfaction of a well-struck winner rolling away harmlessly. 

Dave Fleming made this observation on the air during the start of Game Three of the Women’s Doubles Final at the Toys “R” Us PPA Finals: 

“We love the firepower, but what truly makes Anna Leigh Waters and Anna Bright so special is their defense under siege. They throw the ball back and make you hit another one and another one, and that can be as frustrating as the offense coming at you.”

Bright and Waters this season averaged 15.3 Clean Winners per final, allowing their opponents only 7.7 per match. During their last five finals, it was 18.6 for, and 6 against. They clearly got better as the season went along.

Air-tight defense can be measured another way, when one team does not allow the other any Clean Winners. Since the start of 2023, there have been 285 finals in Men’s, Women’s and Mixed Doubles. Only two times, once in 2023 and in that PPA Finals Women’s match, did a team clamp down and prevent their opponents from having any Clean Winners in two consecutive games. That’s what Bright and Waters did in San Clemente.

Exceptional defense. You know it when you see it, and the statistics back it up.

title: 2026 Carvana PPA Tour Spring Season Produces Record-Breaking Growth Across All Key Business Areas
dek: The Carvana PPA Tour 2026 spring season recently culminated with the thrilling Toys “R” Us PPA Finals in San Clemente, Cali., and the tour’s 10-tournament January-May slate delivered big results Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
The Carvana PPA Tour 2026 spring season recently culminated with the thrilling Toys “R” Us PPA Finals in San Clemente, Cali., and the tour’s 10-tournament January-May slate delivered big results across the board, proving the magnitude and staying power of professional pickleball in the pantheon of mainstream sports entities.

Each key business area produced all-time Carvana PPA Tour records and significant year-over-year growth (vs. the first 10 domestic PPA events of 2025):

Ticket Revenue

  • Ticket revenue was up 58%, year-over-year

Viewership & Fan Engagement

  • The No. 1 and 3 most-watched pro pickleball matches of all-time aired during the 2026 PPA Spring season
    • 791,000 average viewers – Jan. 18, 2026, on CBS (PPA Carvana Masters)
    • 570,000 average viewers – May 2, 2026, on CBS (PPA Atlanta)
  • PBTV event coverage generated 23% year-over-year growth (total of 473 million minutes viewed)
  • Carvana PPA Tour social media accounts have seen a 37% increase in new followers, along with +72% in impressions and +124% in social media engagement year-over-year

Additional Spring 2026 Highlights

  • Apollo Sports Capital leads $225 million investment in Pickleball Inc., parent company of the PPA Tour
  • 2026 SFIA annual report confirms pickleball as America’s fastest-growing sport for the 5th consecutive year; now the fourth-most played sport in the country (over 24 million players)
  • 2025 marked PPA Tour international expansion into Asia and Australia, and 2026 has seen the introduction of additional tournaments in Italy and Canada
  • PPA Athletes ranked in the Top 20 across all disciplines (Singles, Doubles, Mixed Doubles) represent 17 countries

title: Why Diamond Tough technology changes the game
dek: There is a moment every pickleball player knows well. You step onto the court with a brand new paddle. The first drive pops off the face. The ball dips sharply Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
There is a moment every pickleball player knows well.

You step onto the court with a brand new paddle. The first drive pops off the face. The ball dips sharply on a topspin roll. Drops feel soft but precise. Everything responds exactly how you imagined.

For a while, it feels effortless.

Then slowly, something changes. The spin is not quite as sharp. The ball does not bite the same way on resets. The paddle still plays well, but that original edge begins to fade.

It is one of the quiet frustrations of pickleball. Players train, refine technique, and study strategy, yet the surface of their paddle is often working against them as the months go by.

At Six Zero, we believe equipment should grow with the player, not wear them down over time. That belief pushed our engineering team to tackle one of the sport’s most persistent challenges: surface durability and spin retention.

The result is Diamond Tough technology, a surface designed to maintain the spin and texture players rely on long after the first match.

A problem every player understands

Spin has become a defining part of the modern pickleball game. Heavy topspin drives, dipping passing shots, and sharp angle rolls at the kitchen are now common at every level of play.

But spin depends heavily on surface texture.

There are paddles that rely on sprayed grit coatings. They create impressive spin early on, but that texture often breaks down quickly. Players are left wondering why the paddle that felt so sharp out of the box suddenly feels smooth only a few months later.

Raw carbon fiber improved durability, introducing peel ply textures that last longer than spray coatings. Even so, over time the epoxy layer begins to smooth out, reducing the surface friction players rely on.

It is a cycle many players know too well. The paddle performs beautifully at first, then gradually loses its bite.

Six Zero wanted to change that pattern.

Looking beyond traditional materials

When designing Diamond Tough, our goal was simple: create a paddle surface that could maintain its spin characteristics far longer than conventional construction.

The answer came from a material known for its resilience.

Diamonds.

Diamond Tough is a proprietary, patent pending surface technology that infuses industrial grade diamond particles directly into the epoxy and peel ply layer of the carbon fiber face. Instead of sitting on top of the paddle as a coating, these microscopic diamond particles become part of the surface itself.

Under bright light, you can sometimes catch the sparkle across your paddle face. It is subtle, but it reveals the structure beneath. Those particles create a textured surface designed to grip the ball with remarkable consistency.

The goal was never to chase flashy marketing claims. The goal was to solve a problem players feel every time their paddle starts losing spin.

A surface that refreshes itself

One of the most interesting aspects of Diamond Tough is how the surface behaves over time.

Traditional carbon fiber paddles gradually smooth out as the outer epoxy layer wears down. Once that texture fades, the spin potential drops with it.

Diamond Tough was engineered differently.

As the outermost layer wears through regular play, new diamond particles continue to be revealed beneath the surface. The paddle effectively refreshes its own texture as it ages, maintaining the gripping characteristics players depend on.

Think of it like a precision abrasive tool. As the surface works, it continues exposing new edges that keep the ball biting.

For players, this means the paddle they trust in week one can still deliver the same predictable spin months later.

The numbers behind the feel

Innovation is important, but we believe performance should always be measurable.

Independent testing has shown how dramatically Diamond Tough improves surface longevity.

In grit retention testing conducted by Pickleball Effect, the Six Zero Coral paddle retained approximately 95 percent of its original surface roughness after extended testing cycles. 

Additional surface analysis from Matt’s Pickleball measured only a 3.4 percent reduction in surface depth for the Coral Hybrid after heavy wear simulation. Comparable paddles showed degradation between 12 percent and nearly 30 percent.

Those numbers tell a clear story. Diamond Tough surfaces are engineered to maintain their texture significantly longer than conventional designs, with durability that can last up to four times longer than standard raw carbon.

Innovation guided by player experience

At Six Zero, technology is never developed in isolation. Every design decision begins with the same question: does this actually help players perform better over time?

That mindset guided the development of Diamond Tough from the very beginning. For Six Zero Founder Dale Young, the goal was never simply to introduce a new material. It was about solving a problem players experience every time they step on the court.

“Diamond Tough has been developed over the past two years in our R&D lab with a singular focus: dramatically increasing texture life. It’s been a long development journey, and we are extremely proud of the final outcome,” Dale says.

“Seeing Diamond Tough validated not only in controlled lab testing but also on court has been incredibly rewarding. Thousands of customers have now used the technology, and the overwhelmingly positive feedback is a powerful confirmation that the investment was worthwhile.

At the end of the day, creating positive experiences and adding real value for players is what motivates me to continue pushing innovation forward. Delivering meaningful improvements—backed by performance and durability—will always be at the heart of our product development philosophy.”

The result is a technology built not just for launch day performance, but for the many matches that follow.

What players notice on the court

Across the Six Zero community, one theme comes up again and again: consistency.

Players frequently mention that months into using their paddles, the spin still feels reliable. Drives continue to dip. Resets still grip the ball. The paddle behaves the way it did when they first unwrapped it.

One player described putting well over one hundred hours on his Ruby Pro and Coral while still feeling confident generating spin in competitive matches. Another shared that even after more than a hundred hours with his Opal, controlled shots at moderate power still produced the same predictable downward dip at the net.

Those are the moments that matter most to us. Not the marketing claims, but the confidence players feel when their equipment performs exactly how they expect.

Where you will find Diamond Tough

Diamond Tough technology is featured across the entire Six Zero Next Gem™ lineup.

Each paddle in the series incorporates this advanced surface design to help maintain spin consistency and extend the usable lifespan of the paddle. By embedding diamond particles directly into it’s structure, the surface is engineered to preserve its texture and playability long after the initial play sessions.

While each Next Gem™ paddle offers its own balance of power, control, and feel, they all share the same underlying commitment to durability and performance.

Built for the long game

Pickleball is evolving quickly. Players are stronger, faster, and more skilled than ever before. Equipment must keep pace with that progression.

Diamond Tough represents one step in that journey.

It is a surface built to maintain spin longer, perform more consistently, and give players the confidence that their paddle will respond the same way match after match.

Because innovation at Six Zero has always been driven by the players who push the game forward.

It’s time to Go Next Level!

San Clemente, California.

May 10, 2026.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL:  (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (4) Rachel Rohrabacher and Christian Alshon, 11-5, 11-5, 11-5.

  • Johns and Tardio’s 16th title this season, the most of any team in Men’s, Women’s or Mixed Doubles.
  • Tardio is the only PPA Tour player to win all ten tournaments in 2026 in the same event, in this case, Men’s Doubles.

  • Johns and Tardio had more Clean Winners, 23-10.

title: TOYS R US PPA FINALS PRESENTED BY JOOLA STORYLINES (MAY 6-10, 2026)
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: POINTS AWARDED IN EACH DISCIPLINE: HOW THIS FINALS FORMAT WORKS: Each team/player plays every other team/player in their pool. The top 2 advance to the semis. Read more
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • INVITE ONLY: Players had to qualify – top 8 in singles and mixed, top 16 in gender doubles.
  • NATIONAL EYEBALLS AGAIN: National FOX audience on Sunday at 5pm Eastern. 
  • JUMP IN THE POOL: Wednesday through Friday is pool play, top 2 in each of the 2 pools advance to Semifinal Saturday (Pool A winner plays second in Pool B and vice versa). 
  • NO GOAT: Anna Leigh Waters is skipping singles but will play the two doubles events. 
  • BIG BONUS: The FINALS counts as an extra event to add to your points and ranking. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • One of the most picturesque venues in pickleball – breathtaking Life Time San Clemente.
  • Over 1,500 players participating, including a 500 point full pro event for those who did not qualify for the Finals. 
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins at 2pm Eastern Wednesday through Friday and 1pm Eastern Saturday and Sunday. 
  • Exclusive FS1 window 7-9pm Eastern Saturday night. 
  • Exclusive big FOX window 5-7pm Eastern on Sunday. 

POINTS AWARDED IN EACH DISCIPLINE:

  • 300 per round robin win
  • 400 for a semis win
  • 700 for a finals win

HOW THIS FINALS FORMAT WORKS:

Each team/player plays every other team/player in their pool. The top 2 advance to the semis. The winner of pool A plays second place in pool B (and vice versa) on Semifinal Saturday. The two winners then play for gold on Sunday. 

The final standings in each pool are determined in this order:

  1. Greatest number of wins
  2. If 2 teams are tied in wins, head to head will break the tie. 
  3. If 3 teams are tied, ties are broken by head to head sweep, followed by:
    1. Point differential for all matches
    2. Point differential H2H
    3. Point differential against next highest ranked team. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES POOLS:

Player to watch: Kate Fahey: with Anna Leigh Waters out of singles, this is her chance to shine. She played an impressive, grueling final against Waters in Atlanta and should bring tons of confidence to California. 

MEN’S SINGLES POOLS:

Player to watch: Has to be Chris Haworth. Rose to the number 1 ranking, cemented that with the win in Atlanta and handled the hype of Tama town like a pro in beating the youngster to grab that gold. 

MIXED DOUBLES POOLS:

Team to watch: Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin – made the final in Atlanta but were swept in the Finals by Waters/Johns – can they find the level when they did the sweeping in Mesa?

WOMEN’S DOUBLES POOLS:

Team to watch: Parris Todd and Rachel Rohrabacher – they won in Sacramento (without Waters/Bright in the draw) and showed a lot of chemistry, versatility, and high level play – can they bring that to the southern part of the state?

MEN’S DOUBLES POOLS:

Team to watch: Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio are undefeated in 2026. They are the standard – will anyone be able to match it?

title: PARTNERS: The First Reality Docuseries Inside Professional Pickleball Is Here
dek: Watch all six episodes now on the Carvana® PPA Tour YouTube Channel The cameras are rolling, the rivalries are real, and pickleball just got the docuseries it deserves.On May 5, Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Watch all six episodes now on the Carvana® PPA Tour YouTube Channel

The cameras are rolling, the rivalries are real, and pickleball just got the docuseries it deserves.
On May 5, PARTNERS — the first-ever reality docuseries inside professional pickleball — premieres simultaneously on Prime Video, PickleballTV, and the Carvana® PPA Tour YouTube Channel. All six episodes. Dropping at once. No waiting between cliffhangers.
What’s Actually Going On
Pro pickleball has been called a traveling high school: players train together, date each other, party together, then step on court and try to destroy each other. PARTNERS embeds cameras inside that world for the most defining season the sport has ever had.
A few of the storylines you’re about to be obsessed with:

  • Anna Leigh Waters, 18 years old and out-earning the WNBA, dismantles the top women’s doubles team in pro pickleball with a single phone call.
  • Ben Johns — the most decorated man in the sport — walks away from a winning partnership with his own brother to bet on 19-year-old Bolivian phenom Gabe Tardio.
  • Parris Todd and Hunter Johnson turn a very public breakup into the performances of their lives.
  • Federico Staksrud writes “I am the best player in the world” on a piece of paper every single day, and at the World Championships in Dallas, he gets the chance to prove it.
  • Anna Bright says out loud what everyone else is thinking: she wants to steal Anna Leigh’s sparkle.
  • “Hurricane” Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson have one mission: take down the queen.

This isn’t a highlight reel. It’s the feuds, the fallout, the partner swaps, the heartbreaks, and the high-stakes mind games that decide who’s lifting trophies — and who’s getting left behind.

Why It Matters

Pickleball is the fastest-growing sport in America, and Gen Z owns the net. PARTNERS is the first time the sport has been pulled wide open for everyone — from die-hard fans to people who’ve never picked up a paddle.
If you’ve ever wondered what it actually looks like at the top of pro pickleball, this is your front-row seat.

How to Watch

Watch PARTNERS on the Carvana® PPA Tour YouTube Channel

All six episodes. Free. Streaming now.
Also available on Prime Video (free with Prime membership).

PARTNERS is produced by Shutterstock Studios in association with Wavelength Productions LLC, with Dan Bradley (Sprint) as showrunner.

title: Apollo Sports Capital Leads Landmark $225 Million Investment in Pickleball Inc. – New Parent Company of PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball
dek: Pickleball Inc. has become the new parent company of the Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) following a $225 million structured investment led by Apollo Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
Pickleball Inc. has become the new parent company of the Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) following a $225 million structured investment led by Apollo Sports Capital, an investment platform of Apollo (NYSE: APO).

The capital raise results in the largest singularly-operated pickleball ecosystem in existence, integrating professional and amateur pickleball with leading technology, retail, and infrastructure platforms. Pickleball Inc.’s newly-merged business verticals generated over $140 million in 2025 revenue on a combined basis, while setting a host of growth records. Tom Dundon and the Pardoe family will remain majority shareholders in the business, rolling in several additional pickleball assets across facilities, courts, ecommerce, and technology.

“This is a seismic day for the rapidly growing business of pickleball at all levels,” said PPA Tour founder and Pickleball Inc. CEO Connor Pardoe. “This investment allows us to fully integrate the sport into one cohesive ecosystem – uniting professional pickleball, consumer goods, technology, and media under a single, unified platform. By bringing together the best companies in the space, we’re creating an end-to-end experience that serves every pickleballer on their journey, whether they’re a casual enthusiast or a dedicated fanatic. At its core, this is still about building and delivering the culture, fun, and community that define pickleball’s DNA.”

“Pickleball is one of the fastest growing sports in the world, appealing to players and fans of all ages, and we are excited to be making this structured investment,” said Al Tylis, CEO of Apollo Sports Capital. “This is a unique opportunity to support the combination of these assets, effectively reimagining how to create a professional sports league under a single ecosystem and platform for growth. We believe that the Company now has the resources it needs to get to the next level, having already proved itself as the most successful emerging sports league of the past decade.”

Pickleball Inc.’s business momentum, combined with the explosion of the sport at the amateur level – pickleball has been named the fastest-growing sport in America in each of the last five years (24 million players in 2025) and is the fourth-most played sport in the country, per the 2026 SFIA Annual Report – shows the strength of, and opportunities for, the newly combined entity.

The professional sport has been a marquee platform for gender equity, with men and women on court equally during both PPA and MLP events. Additionally, the top 60 women in the sport average over $260,000 in annual salary, the highest average pay in all of professional women’s team sports.

“The continued and dynamic year-over-year growth data has proven without a doubt that pickleball is no longer an emerging sport, and is instead quickly becoming the next tier one sport in America,” said MLP Commissioner Samin Odhwani. “This capital raise will allow us to expand our focus into new and scalable opportunities like content, media, and the development of infrastructure to support our fast growing events.”

The five-person board of Pickleball Inc. includes Al Tylis, Connor Pardoe, Jason Stein, Zubin Mehta, and Brian Levine.

Additional information on Pickleball Inc.’s business verticals, which encompass every level of the sport, from pro players at the very top of the pyramid to casual players enjoying pickleball for the very first time:

Professional Play – Carvana PPA Tour & MLP presented by DoorDash

  • Pro pickleball’s leading tour (fall-spring season) and coed team league (summer season), respectively, with a collection of over 150 signed pro players and a combined year-round event calendar bringing the best pros from around the world to markets across the U.S.
  • Recently established all-time linear viewership records for both PPA (791,000 avg. viewers on CBS, Jan. 18, 2026) and MLP (499,000 avg. viewers on CBS, Aug. 23, 2025)
  • PPA/MLP athletes earn a total of more than $33 million in prize money and payouts ($260,000+ annual avg.)

Retail – Pickleball Central

  • The market-leader in pickleball retail, offering equipment – from paddles to balls to shoes – in addition to accessories and apparel
  • World’s largest pickleball retailer, shipping over 1 million orders since its founding in 2006
  • Omni-channel, with over 100 Pickleball Central pro shops across the United States

Software – Pickleball Play Solutions

  • The software that powers PPA and MLP events – PickleballTournaments.com – in addition to thousands of amateur tournaments and league seasons, annually, with a 90% market share for events and organized play
  • PPS website properties average approximately 5 million visits per month
  • PPS website properties hosted 4,500 tournaments and 2,000 league seasons in 2025

Court Construction – Just Courts

  • The “Official Court Installer” for many prestigious organizations across the pickleball market, including MLP & PPA events, schools, facilities, and community centers

Media – Pickleball.com and Pickleball TV

  • Pickleball.com is the go-to online destination for live scores, news, video highlights, merchandise, tournaments, leagues, clubs, ratings, and clinics, offering the latest updates from across the world of pickleball
  • Pickleball TV, a joint venture with Tennis Channel, is the only 24/7 digital network dedicated to America’s fastest-growing sport, available on YouTube TV and as a FAST channel on a collection of streaming services, bringing fans live coverage of every PPA and MLP event

Investments in Picklr and DUPR

  • Picklr, the leading indoor pickleball facility brand, features over 500 locations worldwide

DUPR, the world’s most accurate pickleball rating, with over 1 million DUPR rated pickleball players participating in matches, building community, and improving their skill level.

title: VEOLIA ATLANTA PICKLEBALL CHAMPIONSHIPS STORYLINES (APRIL 27-MAY 3, 2026)
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: MEN’S SINGLES: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES: POINTS DISTRIBUTION IN ATLANTA:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • SLAM THE DOOR: Last event of the 25/26 season is worth 2,000 points, double an Open.
  • NATIONAL EYEBALLS: National CBS audience on Saturday at 12:30 Eastern. 
  • THEY’RE BAAAAAACK (ALL OF THEM): Waters, Bright, Patriquin, Alshon, Kawamotos, Tuionetoa – all in. 
  • RACING STRIPES: Last chance to qualify for the Finals…who will get in?
  • GOLDIN RETURN: Welcome back Grayson Goldin from a stroke suffered earlier this year. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Final event of the 25/26 season at beautiful Life Time Peachtree Corners.
  • Over 1,700 players participating. 
  • A progressive draw on the pro side, one round per bracket per day.
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins at 10am Eastern Tuesday through Friday & Sunday. 9am start Saturday.  
  • Semifinal Saturday mixed doubles coverage at 12:30 Eastern with the CBS exclusive national 2 hour window. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending medalists: Ben Johns, Connor Garnett, Hunter Johnson
  • Chris Haworth is #1 in the world, can he win as the favorite? Staksrud coming off his win in Sacramento, is the 2 seed. 
  • Ben Johns is not playing singles in this event so he will not defend his title. 
  • Potential R32 thriller: Jack Sock (7) vs. JW Johnson (26)
  • RACE STORYLINE: Can John Lucian Goins (8) hold onto 8th position and qualify? He’s 800 points ahead of Gabe Joseph (9) who sits in 9th. These two could meet in the round of 16. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending medalists: Anna Leigh Waters, Kate Fahey, Parris Todd
  • Waters is the top seed, Fahey the two.  
  • Anna Leigh Waters’ unbeaten streak has reached 698 days at the start of the main draws in ATL. 
  • Potential battle in R32: Brooke Buckner (4) vs. Samantha Parker (29)
  • RACE STORYLINE: Genie Bouchard (10) is 400 points behind Judit Castillo (9) and 11th in the race. Can she put together a huge week and jump into the top 8? 

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Waters/Johns, Tuionetoa/Alshon, Jorja/JW Johnson
  • Waters and Johns top the seeds, the Johnsons are the 2, and Bright/Patriquin are the 3 in the Johnsons’ half.

title: 122-SHOT RALLY in Sacramento!
dek: The longest rally in any PPA Tour final since the start of 2022 happened at the Fasenra Sacramento Open, in the Men’s Doubles final. Let’s take a deep dive into Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
The longest rally in any PPA Tour final since the start of 2022 happened at the Fasenra Sacramento Open, in the Men’s Doubles final. Let’s take a deep dive into a breathtaking two-minute and one-second rally!

Game Three. After splitting the first two games, Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio led JW Johnson and CJ Klinger 5-4-2. The rally started with an ordinary five-shot sequence: Tardio serve, Johnson return, Johns third-shot drive, Klinger volley, Johns fifth-shot drop into the kitchen. Then, 34 dinks, an eight-shot firefight, 67 dinks, and another eight-shot firefight. Yes, 101 dinks in one rally.

After the first five shots, there were 30 dinks before Johnson became involved with a dink of his own. After three more dinks, Klinger started the first firefight, which ended with Tardio resetting a Johnson smash back into the kitchen.

“Wow, wow, wow,” Dave Fleming said on the broadcast.

A 67-dink rally ensued, until Johns initiated a firefight, which ended with a Klinger volley sailing long.

“Yes please… that was sensational!” Fleming said.

Here are some stats: 

Shots: Klinger 48, Johns 33, Tardio 28, Johnson 13.

Dinks: Klinger 42, Johns 27, Tardio 23, Johnson 9.

Klinger hit 78% of his team’s shots in the rally. It was more balanced on the other side of the net, with Johns hitting 54% of his team’s shots.

Johns and Tardio won the point, the game, and the match… a match that included this epic rally.

By the way, this rally was like a tsunami. The six rallies before it and the six rallies after it were all seven shots or less!

title: Championship Sunday Standout Stats from the Fasenra Sacramento Open.
dek: Sacramento, California. April 19, 2026. MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (4) Tyra Black and Eric Oncins def. (1) Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson, 11-7, 6-11, 3-11, 11-8, 11-8. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Sacramento, California.

April 19, 2026.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (4) Tyra Black and Eric Oncins def. (1) Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson, 11-7, 6-11, 3-11, 11-8, 11-8.

  • Black’s second career Mixed Doubles title, both this year, and Oncins’s first.
  • Black and Oncins had zero errors on Serves, Returns, and Third Shots. (Balls hit into the net or out of bounds.) It’s only the third time a team has done this in any final since the start of 2022, and the first time in a five-game final.
  • JW Johnson joins Ben Johns as the only male players with more than 100 career medals.
  • Jorja Johnson had a match-high 12 Dinks into the net or wide.
  • Longest rally: 46 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (2) JW Johnson and CJ Klinger, 11-8, 7-11, 11-6, 11-2.

  • Johns and Tardio’s 14th title this season is the most of any team in Men’s, Women’s or Mixed Doubles.
  • Ben Johns’s 200th final across all disciplines. His record in finals is 181-19.
  • JW Johnson joins Ben Johns as the only male players with more than 100 career medals.
  • All four players had at least ten Clean Winners. Tardio had been involved in each of the last six times that has happened in a Men’s final.
  • Johns and Tardio had fewer Dinks into the net or wide, 10-3.
  • Longest rally: 122 shots, the longest rally in -any- Doubles final since the start of 2022.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (2) Rachel Rohrabacher and Parris Todd def. (1) Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson, 11-5, 6-11, 11-4, 11-6.

  • Rohrabacher’s first title since winning in Milwaukee in November 2024. 
  • Rohrabacher’s ninth career title, and first without Anna Bright as a partner.
  • Todd’s third career title.
  • Rohrabacher/Todd won despite having fewer Clean Winners, 21-11.
  • Longest rally: 77 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (2) Federico Staksrud def. (12) Zane Ford, 11-4, 11-2.

  • Staksrud’s 20th career Singles title.
  • Staksrud’s six titles this season include both Sacramento tournaments.
  • Staksrud’s 20 titles have come against 15 different opponents in the finals.
  • Staksrud had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 17-2.
  • Longest rally: 13 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL:  (1) Kate Fahey def. (2) Kaitlyn Christian, 11-3, 11-0.

  • Fahey’s sixth career title and second this season (both Sacramento events).
  • Three of Christian’s four Return errors were in Game One.
  • Fahey had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 10-4.
  • Longest rally: 9 shots.

title: Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball Partner with Travel Management Platform ‘Engine’
dek: DALLAS – April __, 2026 — Engine, a leading modern business travel platform, has been named the official travel partner of the Carvana Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) Tour and Major Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
• Engine Named Official Travel Partner of the Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash)
  • One-year partnership to streamline business travel bookings for the PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball

DALLAS – April __, 2026 — Engine, a leading modern business travel platform, has been named the official travel partner of the Carvana Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) Tour and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash). This year-long partnership aims to streamline business travel bookings for the PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball, enhancing operational efficiency and maximizing cost savings across over 30 tournaments nationwide.

The PPA Tour, established in 2019, has rapidly grown into the premier professional pickleball circuit, hosting tournaments at the finest pickleball facilities around the world. Founded in 2021, MLP is the preeminent, coed team-based pickleball format in the world. By integrating Engine’s travel management services, the PPA Tour and MLP aim to optimize travel arrangements for its staff, ensuring seamless coordination and focus on delivering high-quality events.

Engine’s modern platform gives companies a single, intuitive place to manage all their travel needs, complete with exclusive, discounted hotel rates and a streamlined booking experience that simplifies every step of the journey.

The Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball both have unique and complex travel needs across their staff, large-scale events, and professional athletes and teams, with a schedule that keeps teams on the road the majority of the year. With Engine, these organizations can take advantage of discounted hotel rates, and staff can book, manage, and track travel and spend across all team travel. Engine takes on the heavy lifting of travel management, including for last minute room blocks, and helps the organizations be more strategic about budgets, travel decisions, and team logistics. Plus, real-time reporting and travel spend tracking make it easier for finance and operations teams to get an accurate and holistic view of travel expenses.

“We are very excited to partner with Engine and utilize their platform to help bring the greatest pickleball competition to tour stops across the country,” said Jacob Cohen, SVP of Partnerships and Revenue for PPA & MLP. “Booking business travel is critical to our tour operations, and this partnership will allow us to further our mission of bringing the world’s best pickleball to our passionate fans.”

“We’re excited to support the sport of Pickleball by taking the complexity out of travel,” said Alex Melamud, CFO at Engine. “Our platform centralizes everything from bookings to budgeting, allowing the league to make smarter, data-driven decisions while teams focus entirely on the competition

This exciting partnership reflects the shared commitment between Engine, the PPA Tour and MLP to creating and utilizing innovative solutions to solve critical business travel needs, in addition to championing the burgeoning sport of professional pickleball. 

About Engine:

Engine is a modern business and group travel platform trusted by over one million travelers. Engine saves businesses time and money through an extensive travel network that connects to nearly every hotel, airline, and car rental company in the U.S. It offers single invoice billing, the flexibility to modify or cancel trips at any time without incurring additional fees, and a unified view of all company travel and spend. Customers rely on Engine to not only make travel easier to manage but also to make it enjoyable for everyone involved. Additionally, Engine helps coordinate room blocks for corporate offsites, sports teams, weddings, family reunions and more to help people get together in person. The company is backed by Telescope Partners, Blackstone, Elefund, and Permira. Learn more at engine.com. 

About Carvana PPA Tour:

Founded in 2019, the Carvana PPA Tour is where pickleball’s top athletes go head-to-head to determine the best male and female players in the world. The Carvana PPA Tour organizes and conducts tournaments at world-class facilities across the country, establishes player rankings, and showcases the world’s best pickleball week in and week out. Inviting amateur players to also compete and “play where the pros play,” the Carvana PPA Tour offers divisions for every age group and skill level. Characterized by a uniquely festive and fun atmosphere, Carvana PPA Tour events deliver unparalleled experiences for fans on-site, including pro player meet-and-greets, clinics, food, beverages, live entertainment, giveaways, games, shopping, and VIP upgrades. For more information, go to www.ppatour.com, and follow us on social: Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn.

About Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash)

Founded in 2021, Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) is the preeminent, coed, team-based professional pickleball league, featuring over 100 of the best athletes across 20 teams, iconic team owners, and the most electric live events and fan experience in the sport. In 2024, MLP and the PPA Tour merged under the newly-formed United Pickleball Association (UPA), bringing together the leading pro pickleball organizations under a single entity. Visit the official website and follow MLP on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube for more information.

Media Contact(s):

Nathan Boschult, PR and Communications Manager, PPA & and MLP

dek: ON MAY 5, THE CARVANA® PPA SERVES UP PARTNERS, THE FIRST REALITY DOCUSERIES INSIDE PROFESSIONAL PICKLEBALL,WHERE THE RIVALRIES ARE REAL AND THE STAKES ARE HIGHER THAN THE SCORE Official Trailer Reveals Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
ON MAY 5, THE CARVANA® PPA SERVES UP PARTNERS, THE FIRST REALITY DOCUSERIES INSIDE PROFESSIONAL PICKLEBALL,
WHERE THE RIVALRIES ARE REAL AND THE STAKES ARE HIGHER THAN THE SCORE

Official Trailer Reveals the Explosive Drama on and off the Court Inside the Sport Where Gen Z Owns the Net

The Six-Part Series Will Simulcast Across Prime Video,
The Carvana® PPA Tour YouTube Channel
And PickleballTV


 

NEW YORK – April 9, 2026 – Pickleball is no longer a recreational pastime. It is a global phenomenon volleying into the mainstream at a speed no one predicted, and it’s getting younger and more competitive by the year.

Now, for the first time, PARTNERS pulls viewers courtside for the fervor, feuds and fallout of professional pickleball. The six-part reality and sports crossover docuseries premieres May 5 on Prime Video in the U.S. at no additional cost with a Prime membership, the Carvana® PPA (Professional Pickleball Association) Tour YouTube Channel and PickleballTV, with all episodes dropping at once.

In pickleball, “love” isn’t even a score. In PARTNERS, it seems to be in short supply, and relationships are as volatile as a heated rally at the net. With insider access to the sport’s biggest threats and most fearless underdogs, the series pulls back the curtain on a tour often described as a traveling high school: Players train together, party together, date each other and show up at the same hotel the morning after a loss or a breakup. Everyone knows everyone’s business. Then they step onto the court, and it’s war. They play to destroy.


At the center of the season is 18-year-old pickleball ingenue Anna Leigh Waters, the undisputed queen of the court who’s outearning anyone in the WNBA. With just one phone call, she dismantles the most dominant women’s doubles team on tour. Choosing a doubles partner is one of the most consequential decisions a professional pickleball player makes, and on the Carvana® PPA Tour it is handled almost entirely through rumors, back-channel conversations and social maneuvering. Anna Leigh’s story is just the beginning:

  • Chasing Anna Leigh’s spotlight is Anna Bright, fierce enough to dissolve one of the tour’s most beloved doubles pairings just to close the gap and candid enough to admit she wants to steal her sparkle.
  • Catherine Parenteau and Rachel Rohrabacher, both left without a partner after Anna Leigh’s phone call, find each other, and nobody sees them coming.
  • Ben Johns, the sport’s most decorated man, walks away from a winning partnership with his own brother to bet everything on 19-year-old Bolivian star Gabe Tardio.
  • After navigating a very public breakup, former sweethearts Parris Todd and Hunter Johnson each channel their heartbreak into the performance of their lives.
  • Federico Staksrud writes on a piece of paper every day that he is the best player in the world. At the World Championships in Dallas, he and partner Hayden Patriquin get their chance to prove it.
  • Matt Wright, 48, plays with a bad back, but paired with Spanish charmer Jaume Martinez-Vich, they’re the last duo anyone wants to face across the net.
  • A competitor so intense she divides the crowd, Kate Fahey is warm and funny off the court and a different person entirely when the ball is in play. She opens up about the mental toll of competing at the highest level.
  • Christian Alshon plays with loud, unfiltered aggression and has beaten Ben enough times to back it up. He and partner Andrei Daescu are pushing men’s pickleball into its most competitive era yet.
  • “Hurricane” Tyra Black and partner Jorja Johnson have just one thing on their minds: taking down the queen.

“People underestimate what these athletes sacrifice,” says PPA CEO Connor Pardoe, who founded the Carvana® PPA Tour at age 25. “Pickleball is everything to them – large parts of their identities, social lives, not to mention their livelihoods. When you embed cameras in an environment like this, you get something you could never script.”

Filmed across the Carvana® PPA Tour’s most defining season, PARTNERS follows a league less than five years old, racing to build notoriety, win over top players and prove just how relentlessly competitive professional pickleball has become.

The series features Anna Leigh Waters, Anna Bright, Ben Johns, Gabe Tardio, Federico Staksrud, Hayden Patriquin, Kate Fahey, Catherine Parenteau, Rachel Rohrabacher, Parris Todd, Hunter Johnson, Jaume Martinez Vich, Lucy Kovalova, Matt Wright, Quang Duong, Tyra Black, Jorja Johnson, Jackie Kawamoto, Jade Kawamoto, Zane Navratil, Christian Alshon, Andrei Daescu, CJ Klinger, J.W. Johnson and Carvana® PPA Tour CEO Connor Pardoe.

PARTNERS is produced by Shutterstock Studios in association with Wavelength Productions LLC. Executive producers include Mark Infante, Michele Gauthier, Aiden Darné and Jon Weidman. Dan Bradley (Sprint) serves as showrunner.

About the Carvana® PPA Tour

The Professional Pickleball Association (PPA Tour), sponsored by Carvana®, is professional pickleball’s premier league, co-founded by Connor Pardoe and Conner Ogden in 2019. The Carvana® PPA Tour has grown to more than 200 contracted players competing across 25 annual events, with prize money surpassing $30 million. The sport is now played in 78 countries.

About Shutterstock Studios

Shutterstock Studios is an award-winning global content engine that develops, produces and distributes premium series, documentaries and branded entertainment designed to extend brand narratives beyond traditional campaigns, push the boundaries of storytelling and move audiences. Combining global first-in-class creativity, agility and next-generation production tools – including a robust suite of AI services for hyperscalers and global brands – Shutterstock Studios delivers work that performs in market, scales globally and never loses sight of the brand. Recognized by the Clios, the Webbys, the Anthem and the Cannes Lions Awards, Shutterstock provides the expertise and reach expected at the highest levels of the industry.

About Wavelength

Wavelength is a globally recognized independent studio with a long list of industry recognition – including Emmys, Tonys, Grammy nominations, and Oscar shortlists. Wavelength’s diverse portfolio includes Academy Award®-shortlisted 32 SOUNDS, Netflix’s RATHER, Venice winner THANK YOU VERY MUCH, ON SWIFT HORSES, Emmy winners FEELS GOOD MAN, ART AND KRIMES BY KRIMES as well as the beloved WON’T YOU BE MY NEIGHBOR. Theater credits include Tony-winning The Outsiders, Tony-nominated The Who’s Tommy and Here Lies Love, and Burlesque. In 2025, Wavelength cemented its commitment to sports and branded entertainment by acquiring Duplex Deli, the production agency founded by Dan Bradley and Jon Weidman. Wavelength’s branded content division brings film-level craft to brand storytelling, partnering with leading brands such as HOKA, Marriott, lululemon, MINI, Uber Eats, Nike, Adidas, and Pepsi. Wavelength was recently honored with 13 Telly Awards, including two gold awards for HOKA’s “Humans of HOKA” and three gold awards for De Beers’ “Talent Unearthed.”

dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES: Point Awards at the Sacramento Open:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • SKIP: No Anna Leigh Waters, Anna Bright, Hayden Patriquin, or Christian Alshon in the draws. 
  • REVERSE: Ben Johns IS playing singles and men’s, not mixed.  
  • NO SPLINTERS: NOT a wooden paddle tournament (which was the case in September of 2025). 
  • TWO-EY: Just two tournaments left for players to qualify for the PPA Finals in San Clemente. 
  • A GRAND:1,000 critical points will be awarded to the winners. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Just two tournaments left until the PPA Finals (this one plus Atlanta Slam). It features a progressive draw, 1 round per bracket per day at Life Time Arden in Sacramento (Year #2 for this venue).
  • Over 900 pro and amateur players are competing. 
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins on Thursday with the round of 16 (starting at 1pm Eastern each day, except for Saturday which starts at noon Eastern).
  • No defending medalists (wooden paddle tournament played here last September). 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Kate Fahey (1) and Kaitlyn Christian (2) are the top seeds. 
  • Christian arrives in Sacramento after a stirring 7 point comeback in game 3 in the Hanoi final vs. Brooke Buckner (down 4-9, won 11-9). 
  • Potential R16 “Houston Open 2024 finals rematch”: Lea Jansen (3) vs. Samantha Parker (15)
  • ROAD TO THE FINALS WATCH: Judit Castillo (5) is 10th in the Race standings so she needs two big weeks to earn a spot in the top 8 and the invite to the finals. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Chris Haworth is the top seed (for the first time) and Federico Staksrud, the 2. 
  • Haworth, Hunter Johnson (3), and Jack Sock (6) all in the same half of the draw…along with…

  • Potential R32 matchup: Johns (11) vs. JW Johnson (23)

  • ROAD TO THE FINALS WATCH 2: Because of his limited singles schedule in the past 12 months, Ben is 23rd in the race to the Finals and mathematically eliminated from qualifying in singles for the Finals.  

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Without Waters/Johns, the Johnson siblings are the top seed, with Daescu/Todd the second seed. 
  • Mad Dropping: New MLP teammates Catherine Parenteau and Max Freeman (9) pair up for the 1st time. 
  • Potential R16: Black/Oncins (4) vs. Jansen/Sock (15)

  • ROAD TO THE FINALS WATCH WOMEN’S PART 2:Kate Fahey is just another 100 points back in 10th and is paired with Federico Staksrud as the 5 seed.

title: Veolia Pickleball National Championships Coming to Cary, North Carolina in The Ultimate Weeklong Celebration of Pro and Amateur Pickleball
dek: DALLAS, April 7, 2026 – The Carvana PPA Tour is thrilled to announce that the Veolia Pickleball National Championships will come to the Tar Heel State later this summer to Read more
author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
• The Veolia Pickleball National Championships, a Carvana PPA Tour Slam, to take place in Cary, N.C. Aug. 31 – Sept. 6, 2026, kicking off the 2026-2027 PPA Tour season
  • Tickets are on sale now, and amateur registration is open for all ages and skill levels
  • Weeklong celebration of pickleball to feature live music, entertainment, engaging fan-friendly activations, exciting pro-led camps and clinics, and so much more 
  • Carvana PPA Tour to turn the Cary Tennis Park into the epicenter of pickleball

DALLAS, April 7, 2026 – The Carvana PPA Tour is thrilled to announce that the Veolia Pickleball National Championships will come to the Tar Heel State later this summer to kick off the 2026-2027 season. The event, which will be held at Cary Tennis Park in Cary, N.C. Aug. 31-Sept. 6, will have a “Slam” designation, offering the largest amount of prize money and ranking points in pro pickleball and will feature the very best athletes in pickleball.

Demand is expected to be high for what will be a celebration of America’s fastest growing sport, as the tournament will include world No. 1’s Anna Leigh Waters (Singles, Doubles, Mixed), Ben Johns (Doubles), Gabe Tardio (Mixed), and Chris Haworth (Singles), alongside North Carolina residents such as world No. 2 Kate Fahey and world No. 4 Brooke Buckner. Other globally ranked local professionals competing will include Durham, N.C. resident Mehvish Safdar and High Point, N.C. resident James Delgado. 

New for 2026, the Veolia Pickleball National Championships will have even more fun for the entire family, including live music concerts, sponsor activations, renowned food and fare, pro-led pickleball camps and clinics, plus much more! 

The Veolia Pickleball National Championships will feature the PPA Tour’s special blend of professional competition where the best players compete for titles and crucial world ranking points, and vast amateur competitions where players of all ages and skill levels can find themselves competing for medals and bragging rights on the pro courts. The tournament is expected to draw a sizable crowd of players so it is encouraged to register as soon as possible to secure a spot in the competition; please click here to register today. For more tournament information, please visit the tournament page here. 

“As pickleball enjoys enormous growth in popularity and participation in the United States and globally, it is critical that we bring the very best of the PPA to the most passionate regions, and North Carolina has shown us year after year how fervent they are about the sport,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder and CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “The PPA brings incredible energy and enthusiasm to all our tournaments, and our Slam tournaments are where we shine the brightest, with unmatched entertainment and excitement for everyone to enjoy. The first-ever Veolia Pickleball National Championships will raise that bar even higher as we turn the Greater Raleigh area into the place where every pickleball fanatic wants to be this summer.” 

“It’s exciting to see how much the PPA Tour experience has grown here in Cary,” said Cary Mayor Harold Weinbrecht. “Our staff does an incredible job making these events special for both players and fans, and our community really shows up. We’re proud to welcome the pickleball world back to Cary.”


“Pickleball is one of the fastest growing sports in America, and there’s no better place for the Carvana PPA Tour to host its national championship than in Cary, North Carolina,” said Scott Dupree, executive director of the Greater Raleigh Sports Alliance (GRSA). “For one week in late summer, the eyes of the rapidly expanding world of pickleball will be focused on Cary Tennis Park. The GRSA is proud to support the PPA and the Town of Cary in bringing this national championship to our market.”

The PPA Tour’s official sustainability partner, Veolia, will be the title sponsor of the weeklong extravaganza, furthering their commitment to making pickleball a sustainable global sport. Veolia makes a unique impact on the sport by curbing the use of plastic water bottles with their water refill stations, and mitigating waste with their used pickleball recycling program.

“Veolia is committed to making pickleball the most sustainable sport in the world and this mission is evidenced by significant investment in the PPA Tour’s biggest events,” said Carrie Griffiths,Veolia’s Executive Vice President, Communications, North America. “We are thrilled to welcome thousands of fans and players to the inaugural Veolia Pickleball National Championships in North Carolina, home to critical Veolia water and environmental technologies locations and hundreds of dedicated employees.”

The 2026 Veolia Pickleball National Championships promises to be an exciting and rewarding experience for seasoned pickleball fans and newbies alike. The first-ever PPA Slam tournament in North Carolina will be a milestone for the sport with the Greater Raleigh area becoming the center of the pro pickleball universe as the 2026-2027 pro pickleball season commences.

title: 02 Sports Insurance Ignites the Future of Pickleball as Official Insurance Provider of Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) and the Professional Pickleball Association (Carvana PPA Tour)
dek: In a landmark move that signals the next evolution of professional pickleball, 02 Sports Insurance today announced a partnership as the Official Insurance Provider of both Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
In a landmark move that signals the next evolution of professional pickleball, 02 Sports Insurance today announced a partnership as the Official Insurance Provider of both Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) and the Professional Pickleball Association (Carvana PPA Tour). This collaboration unites a rapidly rising sport with a forward-thinking insurance leader—setting a new standard for protection, performance, and progress.

Pickleball is not just the fastest-growing sport in North America—it’s a cultural phenomenon. With explosive fan growth, elite competition, and expanding global reach, MLP and the PPA Tour are redefining what modern professional sports look like. Now, with 02 Sports Insurance in their corner, every serve, rally, and championship moment is backed by world-class protection designed for the pace and scale of the game.

“This is more than a partnership—it’s a statement,” said Kandace Kalin, CEO of 02 Sports Insurance. “Pickleball is rewriting the playbook for sports growth, and we’re here to power that momentum. Our mission is to remove uncertainty from the equation, so athletes and organizations can push limits, captivate audiences, and build the future of the sport without hesitation.”

As the Official Insurance Provider, 02 Sports Insurance will deliver a comprehensive, next-generation risk and insurance platform, including:

  • Elite, tailored coverage for league operations, teams, events, and venues
  • Proactive risk intelligence and management to support safe, high-performance environments
  • Scalable solutions designed to grow alongside the leagues’ expanding national and global footprint

The PPA Tour and MLP are excited about this collaboration, which reflects 02’s bold vision to champion innovation across sports and entertainment. By aligning with two of the most influential organizations in pickleball, the company is doubling down on its commitment to empower athletes, enhancing experiences, and help shape one of the most exciting movements in sports today.

The game is changing. The protection behind it is here to stay.

title: Championship Sunday Standout Stats from the Greater Zion Cup.
dek: Ivins, Utah. March 29, 2026. MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (3) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-5, 11-0, 15-13. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Ivins, Utah.

March 29, 2026.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (3) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-5, 11-0, 15-13.

  • Waters and Johns’ 13th title together this season and 62nd overall.
  • Waters and Johns won 25 consecutive points mid-match.
  • Waters is the first player this year to have no errors on Serves, Returns, Thirds, and Dinks in any final. This was done only three times in all of 2025.
  • Bright and Patriquin trailed in Game Three 10-1 before earning two Game Points, then lost 15-13.
  • Longest rally: 38 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (2) Christian Alshon and Hayden Patriquin, 13-11, 3-11, 3-11, 11-2, 11-7.

  • Johns and Tardio’s 13th title this season and 15th together overall.
  • Johns has 61 career Men’s Doubles titles; Tardio has 21.
  • All four players had 10+ Clean Winners. This has happened only four times in any final this season.
  • Alshon and Patriquin lost Game Points in Game One, and lost that game. When teams squander those opportunities in finals, they lose 74% of the time.
  • Patriquin had a match-high eight Dinks into the net or wide.
  • Johns and Tardio had fewer errors on Serves, Returns and Thirds, 14-6.
  • Longest rally: 65 shots.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (4) Kate Fahey and Parris Todd, 11-3, 11-3, 11-0.

  • Bright and Waters’ 13th title this season and 21st overall together.
  • Bright has 30 Doubles titles; Waters has 63.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners, 14-5.
  • Bright and Waters had fewer Volleys into the net, 13-8.
  • Fahey’s first Doubles finals appearance.
  • Fahey was the only player with no Dinking Errors.
  • Longest rally: 51 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (3) Chris Haworth def. (2) Federico Staksrud, 11-9, 11-5.

  • Haworth takes over #1 ranking.
  • Haworth’s sixth career title and fifth this season.
  • Haworth had more Clean Winners, 17-9.
  • Haworth had fewer Serve and Return Errors, 8-0.
  • Longest rally: 17 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Kate Fahey, 8-11, 11-3, 11-2.

  • Waters eleventh title this year, and 62nd in her career.
  • Waters has won 51 consecutive finals appearances.
  • Waters has won the last 24 tournaments she entered.
  • Waters now 15-0 overall and 10-0 in finals vs Fahey.
  • Waters had more Clean Winners, 21-6.
  • Fahey led Game One, 10-0.
  • Longest rally: 18 shots.

For the comprehensive stats of all these gold medal matches, please visit:  facebook.com/groups/propickleballstats
