title: GREATER ZION CUP AT BLACK DESERT RESORT STORYLINES (MARCH 23-29)
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • PIZZA PIZZA: Gabe Tardio has won all 6 men’s doubles titles in 2026 – 5 with Johns, 1 with Daescu. 
  • HOWLING HIS WAY BACK: Will Howells returns from extended injury. 
  • ALTITUDE: 2,860 feet above sea level at the splendid Black Desert Resort – who will dial in quickly – Utah players usually on point. 
  • 3 PACK: Parris Todd won a medal of each type in this tourney in 2025 – mixed gold, singles silver, women’s bronze 
  • CUP & SAUCER: 1,500 points to the winners (one of only 4 Cups) – was an Open in 2025. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Event #7 in 2026 features a progressive draw, 1 round per bracket per day at Black Desert Resort – first PPA tournament at this venue. 
  • Over 1,000 players are competing. 
  • Defending medalists are from the Red Rock Open (3/30/25).
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins on Tuesday with the round of 64 (starting times vary – all Eastern) at 12pm on Tues-Thursday, 1pm Friday, 2pm Saturday, and 12pm Sunday.
  • FS1 windows from 7-9pm Eastern Friday and 8-10pm Eastern Saturday. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Anna Leigh Waters, Parris Todd, Lea Jansen
  • Anna Leigh Waters (1) and Kate Fahey (2) are the top seeds. 
  • Potential R16: Catherine Parenteau (6) vs. Kiora Kunimoto (11)
  • Potential QF: Brooke Buckner (4) vs. Lea Jansen (5) 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Anna Leigh Waters – when singles starts her unbeaten streak will be at 664 days. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Hunter Johnson, Jack Sock, Connor Garnett
  • Hunter Johnson is the top seed and Federico Staksrud (2). 
  • R64 can’t miss matchup: Tyson McGuffin (34) vs. JW Johnson (28)
  • Potential R32: Jack Sock (7) vs. Matthew Barlow (32) – back after semis run in Mesa. 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Federico Staksrud (2) – church was back in session as he roared back to take the title in Texas after dropping game 1. 

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Todd/Bar, Parenteau/Alshon, Jorja and JW Johnson 
  • Waters/Johns are the top seed, the Johnson siblings are the 2. 
  • Anna Leigh Waters only played singles and women’s doubles in 2025 – Ben Johns was not in the tourney. 
  • Jorja and JW Johnson have a single bronze medal in 2026, that’s it. 
  • Potential R32 big time matchup: Staksrud/Fahey (9) vs. Sock/Jansen (19)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Oncins/Pisnik (8) – made a huge run to the Final in Newport, can they get back to that form in Utah?

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Parenteau/Waters, Jones/Tuionetoa, Rohrabacher/Todd
  • Waters and Bright are the (1) seed, Jorja Johnson and Tyra Black are the second seed
  • Alix Truong comes off a stirring run to the Finals in Texas and is paired with Zoey Wang as the 6 seed. 
  • Millie Rane was thisclose to her first PPA medal, falling 11-9 in the 3rd in the bronze match – she’s paired with Tina Pisnik (8) this week. 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Jorja Johnson and Hurricane Tyra Black (2) – tough loss in front of the Flash Mob in Dallas, can they rebound? 

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Alshon/Daescu, Patriquin/Staksrud, Johnson/Klinger
  • Top seed is Johns and Tardio, the 2 seed is Alshon/Patriquin. 
  • Tardio has taken over the #1 ranking from Ben Johns. 
  • Howells returns to men’s doubles paired with his New Jersey 5s teammate Noe Khlif as the 13 seed. 
  • Riley Newman returns after a couple of tournaments off as the 9 seed with Armaan Bhatia. 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: THE FIELD – can anyone stop Gabe?

dek: McKinney, Texas. March 15, 2026. MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (3) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-4, 9-11, 11-5, 11-6. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
McKinney, Texas.

March 15, 2026.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (3) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-4, 9-11, 11-5, 11-6.

  • Waters and Johns’ 61st title together and 12th this season.
  • Waters hit 21 Third Shot Drops before her only Third Shot Drive.
  • Patriquin had the most Clean Winners, 16.
  • Patriquin had the most Serve/Return/Thirds Errors, 9, and the most Volleys into the net, 12.
  • Longest rally: 44 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (4) Andrei Daescu and Federico Staksrud, 11-0, 12-10. 11-7.

  • Johns and Tardio’s 14th title together and 12th this season.
  • Game Three had 74% Third Shot Drives to counter windy conditions.
  • Johns and Tardio had more Clean Winners, 20-10.
  • Tardio had no Dinks into the net or wide.
  • Staksrud had no errors on Dinks, Serves, Returns, or Thirds. 
  • Longest rally: 44 shots.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (4) Parris Todd and Alix Truong, 11-2, 11-6, 11-4.

  • Bright and Waters’ 20th title together and 12th this season.
  • Bright and Waters now have a career match record of 99-2.
  • Truong’s first PPA Tour final.
  • Bright had no errors on Serves/Returns/Thirds.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners, 23-4.
  • Longest rally: 57 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Federico Staksrud def. (2) Chris Haworth, 2-11, 11-5, 11-5.

  • Staksrud’s 19th career title and fifth this season.
  • Staksrud led Game Three 6-5 at the change-over, won 11-5.
  • Staksrud had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 16-4.
  • Longest rally: 13 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Kate Fahey, 11-1, 11-6.

  • Completed Waters’ 42nd career Triple Crown.
  • Waters’ 61st career title and tenth this season.
  • Waters has won fifty consecutive gold medal matches.
  • Waters is now 14-0 in her career vs. Fahey.
  • Waters had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 14-8.
  • Longest rally: 11 shots.

dek: Newport Beach, California. March 8, 2026. MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (10) Tina Pisnik and Eric Oncins, 11-4, 11-2, 12-10. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Newport Beach, California.

March 8, 2026.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (10) Tina Pisnik and Eric Oncins, 11-4, 11-2, 12-10.

  • Waters and Johns have never failed to win Mixed Doubles gold together in consecutive tournaments. That covers 66 tournaments since they joined forces at Desert Ridge in January 2022.
  • Waters and Johns’s 60th title together and eleventh this season.
  • Waters and Johns had fewer Dinks into the net or wide, 10-2.
  • Longest rally: 42 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (2) Christian Alshon and Hayden Patriquin, 11-6, 11-2, 3-11, 11-8.

  • Johns and Tardio’s 13th title together and eleventh this season.
  • Johns and Tardio had fewer Return errors, 7-2.
  • Longest rally: 35 shots.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (3) Rachel Rohrabacher and Parris Todd, 11-4, 11-5, 11-3.

  • Bright and Waters’ 19th title together and eleventh this season.
  • Bright is now third all-time with 33 overall career Women’s titles.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners, 21-9.
  • Bright and Waters had fewer Volleys into the net, 20-10.
  • Bright and Waters allowed only 32 points in 11 games in this tournament.
  • Longest rally: 53 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Hunter Johnson def. (2) Federico Staksrud, 12-10, 11-9.

  • Johnson’s eighth career title and third this season.
  • Staksrud had six Return errors, including Match Point.
  • Longest rally: 12 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (5) Lea Jansen, 11-2, 11-1.

  • Waters 60th career title and ninth this season.
  • Waters is 15-1 lifetime in finals against Lea Jansen. Her one win was in June 2021.
  • Waters has won the last 22 tournaments that she has entered, dating back to her loss to Salome Devidze in Dallas, May 30, 2024.
  • Waters had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 12-3.
  • Longest rally: 12 shots.

For the comprehensive stats of all these gold medal matches, please visit:  facebook.com/groups/propickleballstats

title: Carvana PPA Tour and JOMA Sport Announces Groundbreaking Footwear Partnership
dek: DALLAS – March 5, 2026 – The Carvana PPA Tour and JOMA Sport are excited to announce that JOMA Sport will become the Official Footwear Partner of the Carvana PPA Read more
author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
DALLAS – March 5, 2026 – The Carvana PPA Tour and JOMA Sport are excited to announce that JOMA Sport will become the Official Footwear Partner of the Carvana PPA Tour. This partnership will further accentuate JOMA Sport’s commitment to pickleball, the fastest growing sport in America, and provide the Carvana PPA Tour with world-class athletic footwear to complement the world-class pickleball seen only at Carvana PPA Tour tournaments. 

The Carvana PPA Tour, established in 2019, has rapidly grown into the premier professional pickleball circuit, hosting tournaments at the finest pickleball facilities globally. The partnership reflects the shared commitment between the Carvana PPA Tour and JOMA Sport to meet the rapidly increasing demand for technologically advanced pickleball gear. 

“We couldn’t be happier to partner with JOMA Sport as our Official Footwear Partner,” says Connor Pardoe, Founder & CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “The Carvana PPA Tour is the pinnacle of pro pickleball and JOMA Sport’s commitment is further testament to the strength and staying power of pickleball on the global sports stage.”

“At Joma, we continue working to offer the best product with constant technological evolution and a daily commitment to providing the best to those who give their all in their sport,” said Marina López, managing director of Joma Sport S.A. “That’s why we are delighted to collaborate with PPA and are excited to support them providing the official footwear. This collaboration represents a fundamental step for Joma Sport in pickleball, and we are honoured to be the event’s official partner. A commitment to excellence and an ambition to offer the best are fundamental characteristics of Joma’s philosophy, which we share with PPA.”

With a shared desire to foundationally build the sport of pickleball on a global stage, the Carvana PPA Tour and JOMA Sport are meeting the needs of professionals and amateur players alike in providing high-quality footwear for high-quality competition.

dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • BROOMS: Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin swept Ben Johns and Anna Leigh Waters in the mixed final in Mesa – is this a one off or a sign of things to come? NOTE: on opposite sides of the draw in Newport. 
  • 643: Number of days since Waters lost a singles match.  
  • FEEL A DRAFT? What impact will the Major League Pickleball draft have on players?
  • OUT: Catherine Parenteau is not in the tournament and Ben Johns is just playing doubles events.  
  • OPEN IT UP: 1,000 points to the winners. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Event #5 in 20226 features a progressive draw, 1 round per bracket per day at the Tennis & Pickleball Club at Newport Beach. The PPA was last in Newport in April of 2023 for a doubles only event.  
  • Over 1,300 pro and amateur players are competing. 
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins on Thursday with the round of 16 (starting at 1pm Eastern each day).
  • No defending medalists. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Anna Leigh Waters (1) and Kate Fahey (2) are the top seeds. 
  • Genie Bouchard is not in the tournament – she’s off to a strong start in singles in ‘26, including a win over Fahey.
  • Can Mari Humberg (21) follow up her QF run in Mesa which included a win over Kaitlin Christian?
  • Potential R16 matchup: Lea Jansen (5) vs. Kiora Kunimoto (10)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Waters – is destroying everything in her path in singles, winning gold 11-3, 11-1 in Mesa over the 2 seed Fahey. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Hunter Johnson is the top seed and Federico Staksrud (2). 
  • Mesa Cinderella story Matthew Barlow (made the semis) is not in the draw. 
  • Can’t miss R64 matchup: JW Johnson (26) vs. Tyson McGuffin (36) 
  • Potential R32: Noe Khlif (11) vs. Eric Oncins (20)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Chris Haworth (3) – stopped Ben Johns’ run in the final in Mesa and has earned his highest seed yet on the PPA tour – the 3. 

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Waters/Johns are the top seed, the Johnson siblings are the 2. 
  • Wow, what a new team: Alix Truong/Christian Alshon (4)
  • Wow, what a new team, part 2: Hurricane Tyra Black/Noe Khlif (6) 
  • Wow, what a new team, part 3: Rachel Rohrabacher/Gabe Tardio (7) 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin (3) – cannot have more confidence after the gold medal win in Mesa. 

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Waters and Bright are the (1) seed, Jorja Johnson and Tyra Black are the second seed.
  • Wow, what a “new” team: Parris Todd and Rachel Rohrabacher (3) play together for the 2nd time. 
  • Judit Castillo and Genie Erokhina (14) are paired again after a sensational semi-final run in Mesa – could have a R16 matchup with Todd/Rohrabacher. 
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Black and Johnson – as the two seed (and potentially re-united MLP teammates post draft?) will they make another final and push (or beat) Waters/Bright? 

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Top seed is Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio, the 2 seed is Christian Alshon/Hayden Patriquin. 
  • Potential R16: Ge/Garnett (8) vs. Sock/Tellez (10)
  • Potential R16: Martinez Vich/Devilliers (6) vs. Khlif/Koller (9)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Johns and Tardio (1) – they are the men’s doubles standard until knocked from their throne (and more than once). Boast a 71-4 overall record.

title: Carvana PPA Tour Announces 2026-2027 Schedule featuring Marquee U.S. and International Events
dek: DALLAS, (Feb. 24, 2026) – The Carvana PPA Tour today announces the full 2026-2027 season schedule, which includes the return of iconic events such as the Pickleball World Championships in Read more
author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
• Split-year U.S. calendar bookended by the Veolia Pickleball National Championships and the PPA Finals, with the Pickleball World Championships returning to Dallas in November
  • New season welcomes largest international presence in PPA history across PPA Asia, PPA Australia, PPA Canada and PPA Italy
  • New U.S. locations include tour stops in Chicago and Malibu
  • PPA Challenger Series to feature an anticipated 20 events

DALLAS, (Feb. 24, 2026) –  The Carvana PPA Tour today announces the full 2026-2027 season schedule, which includes the return of iconic events such as the Pickleball World Championships in Dallas, Texas, and the PPA Finals in San Clemente, California, along with highly-anticipated tournaments in Kuala Lumpur, Brisbane and Hong Kong. Kicking off August 31st with the Veolia Pickleball National Championships (in a soon-to-be announced, pickleball-obsessed location), the season of PPA Tour events worth 1000+ ranking points will span coast to coast with 20 tournaments played in prominent locations such as Chicago, Las Vegas, Dallas and many more. 

The 2026-2027 global season on the PPA Tour begins as soon as the 2026 PPA Finals conclude, with opportunities for pros and aspiring pros to earn experience and valuable ranking points in international events and PPA Challenger events. The season also welcomes the introduction of PPA Canada and PPA Italy, who will be hosting PPA 125 and 250 events in Vancouver, Ottawa, Toronto, Portoroz (Slovenia), Brescia and more to be announced. The growth and success of professional pickleball continues in Asia and Australia, as well – the PPA Asia season will feature the most ranking points up for grabs for pros in its history, and PPA Australia will host a record-setting Australian Pickleball Open with a $500,000 prize pool. All points earned at any tournament under the PPA umbrella count towards a unified global ranking. 

View the most complete and up-to-date schedule at PPATour.com.

“The Carvana PPA Tour has seen incredible growth since our founding in 2019, and this streamlined season is further evidence of the arrival of pickleball on the professional sports stage,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder & CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “The 2026-2027 season will provide unbelievable excitement as we continue to build on the legacy and prestige of mainstay tournaments such as the Pickleball World Championships and the PPA Finals, while adding incredible new U.S. tour stops in Chicago and Malibu, plus running our most robust international schedule yet with more than 25 international events across PPA Asia, Australia, Canada and Italy. There is opportunity for every pro and aspiring pro to compete and earn their way onto the biggest stage of pro pickleball.”

The Carvana PPA Tour has experienced exceptional growth since its inception, seeing historic crowds and record-breaking television broadcast windows. The recent live CBS broadcast of the Carvana PPA Masters became the most-viewed pickleball event of any kind on any network, with its audience peaking at over 1 million viewers. The 2026 Carvana Mesa Cup, which concluded this past weekend, also broke ticketing records – becoming the highest-grossing PPA event outside of Worlds. These moments highlight the continued and consistent growth of the sport, proving the legitimacy and sustainability of professional pickleball as a mainstream sports product.

Complimenting the exceptional growth of the Carvana PPA Tour, the professional game is digging into its grassroots to find and promote the best young talent in the country via the PPA Challenger Series, a pipeline to the pinnacle of professional pickleball. The most comprehensive season yet on the PPA Challenger Series, which seeks to nurture emerging pro talent, is shaping up across the U.S., with an anticipated 20 tournaments worth valuable PPA ranking points and experience. 

Between a broadened PPA Challenger Series, a refreshed Carvana PPA Tour schedule, and even more exciting international tournaments, the health of professional pickleball has never been stronger. The 2026-2027 PPA calendar takes significant steps forward in the evolution of pickleball as a professional sport, bringing the sport’s best players and tournaments to new markets across the globe.

title: Championship Sunday Standout Stats from the Carvana Mesa Cup
dek: Mesa, Arizona. February 22, 2026. . MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (2) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin def. (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns, 11-8, 11-9, 11-3. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Mesa, Arizona. February 22, 2026.

.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (2) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin def.  (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns,  11-8, 11-9, 11-3.

  • First title for Bright and Patriquin as a team.
  • Bright has five career Mixed Doubles titles, all with different partners.
  • Bright has been part of four teams to beat Waters and Johns. 
  • Waters and Johns had won their last eleven tournaments together.
  • Bright and Patriquin had more Clean Winners, 18-3.
  • Bright had no errors on Serves/Returns/Thirds.
  • Longest rally: 38 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (2) Christian Alshon and Hayden Patriquin, 8-11, 11-6, 11-8, 13-11.

  • Tenth title this season for Johns and Tardio.
  • Johns and Tardio had more Clean Winners, 27-19.
  • Tardio had no Dinks into the net or wide.
  • Johns and Tardio won Game Four after trailing 7-0-2.
  • Longest rally: 59 shots.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson, 11-1, 13-11, 11-7.

  • Waters’ 60th Women’s Doubles title.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners, 14-8.
  • Bright and Waters had fewer errors on Dinks, Serves, Returns and Thirds, 9-3.
  • Black hit 46 Third Shots; Johnson hit 7.
  • Longest rally: 43 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (4) Chris Haworth def. (10) Ben Johns, 11-6, 11-6.

  • Haworth’s fifth career PPA title.
  • Johns had won 12 straight finals appearances, dating back to Sept. 2023 (Cincy).
  • Haworth had more Clean Winners, 15-5.
  • Johns had five Return errors.
  • Longest rally: 18 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Kate Fahey, 11-3, 11-1.

  • Waters’ 59th career Singles title, and eighth this season.
  • Waters is now 13-0 all-time against Fahey.
  • Waters has won at Mesa five straight years.
  • Waters is 48-0 in Finals since losing in June 2022 (Todd, Orange County).
  • Waters had more Clean Winners (10-3), and had no errors on Serves or Returns.
  • Longest rally: 13 shots.

.

For the comprehensive stats of all these gold medal matches, please visit:  facebook.com/groups/propickleballstats

  • Third career silver medal for Bouchard.
  • Christian had more Clean Winners, 19-10.
  • Christian had fewer Serve & Return Errors, 17-12.
  • Longest rally: 10 shots.

.

For the comprehensive stats of all these gold medal matches, please visit:  facebook.com/groups/propickleballstats

title: STORYLINES FOR THE CARVANA MESA CUP (FEB 16-22, 2026)

author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5:

  • BACK TO THE START: PPA Tour started in Mesa, AZ in February of 2020 (at a different venue).
  • HE’S BAAAAAACK, PART 1: Ben Johns is playing singles for the first time in 2026.
  • HE’S BAAAAAACK, PART 2: Jack Sock returns in all 3 disciplines from injury.
  • SHE’S BAAAAAACK: Anna Leigh Waters is in the singles draw after sitting out the last 2 events.
  • OUR CUP RUNNETH OVER: 1,500 points to the winners (one of only 4 Cups).

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Event #4 in 20226 features a progressive draw, 1 round per bracket per day at the Arizona Athletic Grounds.
  • Over 1,600 players are competing.
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins on Tuesday with the round of 64 (starting at 12pm Eastern each day).
  • FS1 windows from 6-8pm Eastern Thursday and Friday and a Tennis Channel window 12-4 EST on Sunday.

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Anna Leigh Waters, Brooke Buckner, Kate Fahey
  • Anna Leigh Waters (1) and Kate Fahey (2) are the top seeds.
  • Potential R16: Catherine Parenteau (6) vs. Jorja Johnson (12)
  • Potential QF: Brooke Buckner (4) vs. Lea Jansen (5)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Genie Bouchard (8) – huge run in Cape Coral, can she build on it in AZ?

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Ben Johns, Hunter Johnson, Federico Staksrud
  • Hunter Johnson is the top seed and Federico Staksrud (2).
  • Potential R32: Chris Haworth (4), returning from the flu vs. JW Johnson (28)
  • Potential R32: Jack Sock (7) vs. Donald Young (29)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Ben Johns (10), is the defending champion and will be motivated as he makes his 2026 singles debut.
  • BONUS NOTE: To win the tournament, this is the potential path for Ben Johns: R32 Freeman, R16 Garnett, QF Staksrud, SF Alshon, Finals Hunter Johnson.

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Jorja and JW Johnson, Bright/Bar, Waters/Johns
  • Waters/Johns are the top seed, the Johnson siblings are the 2.
  • Potential R16: Rohrabacher/Alshon (5) vs. Todd/Bar (10)
  • Potential R16: Fahey/Staksrud (7) vs. Pisnik/Khlif (9)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Andrei Daescu (4) and Hurricane Tyra Black – first time partners are a serious medal threat.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Parenteau/Waters, Bright/Rohrabacher, Jorja Johnson/Viv Glozman
  • Waters and Bright are the (1) seed, Jorja Johnson and Tyra Black are the second seed
  • Potential QF: Fahey/Todd (4) vs. Pisnik/Schneemann (6)
  • Potential QF: Waters/Bright (1) vs. Tuionetoa/Dizon (5)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Kate Fahey and Parris Todd (4) – first time partners looking to hit the podium.

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Alshon/Daescu, Johns/Tardio, Tellez/Frazier
  • Top seed is Johns and Tardio (partnership started here in ‘25), the 2 seed is Alshon/Patriquin.
  • Potential R16: Bar/Devilliers (6) vs. Sock/Tellez (10)
  • Potential QF: Daescu/Staksrud (3) vs. Oncins/Frazier (5)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Alshon/Patriquin (2) – Alshon won in 2025 with Daescu, can he double down with Big H?

title: Powerball joins PPA State Championship Series as Title Sponsor
dek: DALLAS, Feb. 9, 2026 – The Professional Pickleball Association (PPA Tour) is thrilled to announce Powerball® as the official title sponsor for the Pickleball State Championship Series, a nationwide tournament Read more
author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
DALLAS, Feb. 9, 2026 – The Professional Pickleball Association (PPA Tour) is thrilled to announce Powerball® as the official title sponsor for the Pickleball State Championship Series, a nationwide tournament series that culminates at the Pickleball World Championships, the marquee event in the sport of pickleball.

The series will now officially be known as the “Powerball Pickleball State Championship Series” across all states.

The Powerball Pickleball State Championship Series features more than 55 tournaments across all 50 states, with some states hosting multiple events.  The series gives amateur players of all ages and skill levels the opportunity to compete within their respective divisions in each state’s amateur championship. Gold medalists in each state who earn the title of state champion, will receive automatic qualification into the state champions brackets of the Pickleball World Championships, held in early November.

The Championship court at the Pickleball World Championships, where the world’s top pro pickleball players will compete for gold, will also be known as the “Powerball Championship Court.”

“This partnership with Powerball manifests critical investment in elemental pickleball across America and is a milestone for local, amateur pickleball in every state,” said PPA Founder & CEO Connor Pardoe. “This sport is built on a strong foundation of community, grassroots play and the Powerball Pickleball State Championship Series is central in keeping true to that spirit.”

“For more than three decades, Powerball has inspired people to dream big and imagine what’s possible,” said Powerball Product Group Chair and Iowa Lottery CEO Matt Strawn. “Through the Powerball Pickleball State Championship Series, we’re proud to bring that same spirit of opportunity to athletes across the country – giving them a chance to chase their own championship dreams.”

Powerball’s title sponsorship of the Pickleball State Championship Series aligns with its commitment to supporting local services and programs everywhere the game is sold. More than half of all proceeds from a $2 Powerball ticket stay in the jurisdiction where it was sold to fund good causes, ranging from education to support for veterans. Since its inception in 1992, Powerball has generated more than $38 billion for good causes supported by U.S. lotteries. 

This partnership between Powerball and the PPA highlights a shared dedication to fostering community engagement and promoting active lifestyles through America’s fastest growing sport. The Powerball  Pickleball State Championship Series will continue to grow and amplify the sport of pickleball by showcasing and rewarding the very best pickleball tournament directors and players in the country. 

The PPA was assisted by PIVOT Agency, its sponsorship sales agency of record, in the development of this partnership. 

###

About Powerball

For more than 33 years, Powerball® has helped U.S. lotteries generate funds for good causes, raising more than $38 billion to support education, veterans’ services, parks and recreation, and other essential programs.  More than half of the proceeds from every $2 Powerball ticket stay in the jurisdiction where the ticket was sold. 

Powerball tickets are $2 per play and are sold in 45 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Drawings are held every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET and are broadcast live from the Florida Lottery draw studio in Tallahassee and livestreamed on Powerball.com.

About Carvana PPA Tour:

Founded in 2019, the Carvana PPA Tour is where pickleball’s top athletes go head-to-head to determine the best male and female players in the world. The Carvana PPA Tour organizes and conducts tournaments at world-class facilities across the country, establishes player rankings, and showcases the world’s best pickleball week in and week out. Inviting amateur players to also compete and “play where the pros play,” the Carvana PPA Tour offers divisions for every age group and skill level. Characterized by a uniquely festive and fun atmosphere, Carvana PPA Tour events deliver unparalleled experiences for fans on-site, including pro player meet-and-greets, clinics, food, beverages, live entertainment, giveaways, games, shopping, and VIP upgrades. For more information, go to www.ppatour.com, and follow us on social: Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn.

title: STORYLINES FOR THE ZIMMER BIOMET CAPE CORAL OPEN (FEB 9-15, 2026)
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5:

  • URGENT CARE: Many pros were fighting illness in Minnesota – will everyone be 100% in Cape Coral?
  • ROLLER COASTER TEMPS: From 80s at the Masters to negatives in Minny to 75 and mostly sunny in FLA.
  • NOT SINGULARLY FOCUSED: Anna Leigh Waters, Ben Johns, & Parris Todd sitting out singles.
  • 30/30/30 CLUB: Anna Bright is one gold from having at least 30 golds, silvers, and bronzes.
  • OPEN IT UP: 1,000 points to the winners.

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Year #2 at The Courts in Cape Coral, Florida. 2025 event was held in March.
  • Event #3 in 2026 features a progressive draw, one round per bracket per day.
  • Coverage on PickleballTV begins with the round of 16, starting at 10am Eastern Thursday to Sunday.

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Anna Leigh Waters, Lea Jansen, Kate Fahey
  • Kate Fahey (1) and Kaitlyn Christian (2) are the top seeds.
  • Can Liz Truluck (8) keep up her strong play after a run to bronze at the Masters?
  • 17 year old Kiora Kunimoto (17) made the semis in MN, could have a tough R32 match vs. Devidze (12).
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Kate Fahey (1) – wears the one next to her name, can she take it to a title with ALW out of the draw?

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Christian Alshon, Jaume Martinez Vich, John Lucian Goins
  • Hunter Johnson is the top seed and Federico Staksrud (2).
  • Haworth is now the 4 seed, has earned his way there from the 57 seed in mid 2025.
  • Goins (9) started his ascent in singles here in 2025, could face Bellamy (6) in R16.
  • Great R64 youth vs. experience matchup: Shimabukuro (29) vs. McGuffin (40)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Hunter Johnson (1) – won with the one seed in MN, confident player heading to FLA.

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Waters/Johns, Bright/JW Johnson, Parenteau/Alshon
  • Waters/Johns return as the 1 seed, the Johnsons return as the 2 seed (neither team played in MN).
  • Hurricane Tyra Black, after winning in MN, is paired with the lefty Mo Alhouni as the 11 seed.
  • Jade Kawamoto and Andrei Daescu are a dangerous 6 seed as 1st time partners.
  • Dekel Bar and Parris Todd (10) are 5-0 as a team, having won their only tourney – Red Rock Open in 2025.
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Rachel Rohrabacher/Christian Alshon (4) – Alshon won in MN with Black, can he make it two in a row with Rohrabacher and his “take over the court” style?

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Parenteau/Waters, Bright/Rohrabacher, Black/Jones
  • Waters and Bright are the (1) seed, Parenteau and Rohrabacher (2) are the second seed
  • Extremely athletic first time partners Fahey and Schneemann (6) look to make a run.
  • Potential quarterfinal to watch: Kawamoto sisters (4) vs. Todd/Truong (5)
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Jorja Johnson and Tyra Black (3) – back together and have the firepower to take the title.

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Daescu/Johns, Alshon/Staksrud, JW Johnson/Klinger
  • Top seed is Johns and Tardio, the 2 seed is Alshon/Patriquin.
  • Alshon/Patriquin come off a heartbreaking loss to Tardio/Daescu in MN, dropping game 5 12-10.
  • Potential Q to watch:(4) JW Johnson/Klinger vs. (7) Khlif/Tellez
  • WATCH OUT FOR: Johns and Tardio who have traded the #1 overall ranking back & forth over the past 2 weeks and are back together after Johns skipped MN.

dek: Lakeville, Minnesota January 27, 2026 MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (2) Tyra Black and Christian Alshon def. (1) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-8, 11-9, 11-6. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Andrei Daescu Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Lakeville, Minnesota

January 27, 2026

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (2) Tyra Black and Christian Alshon def. (1) Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, 11-8, 11-9, 11-6.
  • First Mixed Doubles gold medals for both Black and Alshon.
  • Alshon’s first Mixed Doubles gold medal after eight straight silvers.
  • Alshon hit 63 of his team’s 66 Third Shots.
  • Black had no errors on Serves or Returns.
  • Longest rally: 34 shots.
MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Andrei Daescu and Gabe Tardio def. (2) Christian Alshon and Hayden Patriquin, 1-11, 14-12, 10-12, 11-8, 12-10.  
  • Daescu’s ninth men’s Doubles title; Tardio’s 16th. 
  • Daescu and Tardio trailed 8-3 in Game Five.
  • All four players had ten-or-more Clean Winners for the first time in a final since last August in Las Vegas.
  • Patriquin’s 24 Clean Winners was the most by a player in a Men’s Doubles final since Ben Johns had 25 at the Masters two years ago.
  • Scoring three points or fewer in Game One and still winning a Gender or Mixed Doubles final? It happened only twice last year.
  • Longest rally: 38 shots.
WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (3) Tyra Black and Parris Todd, 11-1, 6-11, 11-3, 11-5.
  • Bright and Waters’ 16th title together.
  • Bright’s 25th Women’s Doubles title; Waters’ 58th.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners, 19-9.
  • There were five Clean Winners in Game One. Waters had all five.
  • Black had no errors on Serves, Returns and Thirds.
  • Longest rally: 62 shots.
MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Hunter Johnson def. (5) Christopher Haworth, 11-6, 11-0. 
  • Johnson’s seventh career title is third all-time behind Ben Johns (42) and Federico Staksrud (17). It also broke a tie at six with JW Johnson and Tyson McGuffin.
  • Haworth was trying to be the first player to win three consecutive Men’s Singles titles since Ben Johns did it in Dec. ’22-Feb. ’23.
  • Johnson had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 16-4.
  • Longest rally: 20 shots. (Match point).
WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (4) Parris Todd def. (3) Lea Jansen, 11-5, 11-5. 
  • Todd’s fourth career title, and first since Bristol last August.
  • Jansen’s first final since the Cape Coral Open last March.
  • Todd had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 13-3.
  • Longest rally: 19 shots.

title: Building the On-Ramp to Pickleball
dek: How Big Dill Pickleball captured the next generation of pickleball players with approachable, durable gear. On community courts and suburban driveways across the country, the first paddle many new players Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
How Big Dill Pickleball captured the next generation of pickleball players with approachable, durable gear.

On community courts and suburban driveways across the country, the first paddle many new players pick up will never see a professional tournament. It will not be built for elite spin rates or baseline drives. But for the Professional Pickleball Association and the broader competitive community, those early moments still matter deeply.

“Every great player starts in a completely ordinary place,” Big Dill Pickleball Co. founder and CEO Katy Luxem said. “Usually with a borrowed paddle, a few friends, and absolutely no idea how much the game is about to matter to them.”

For the PPA circuit, that recreational base is the pipeline. It is where tomorrow’s competitive players begin. Big Dill Pickleball Co. has shaped its business around capturing that next generation with gear that is approachable, durable, and serious enough to grow with new players as their skill develops.

Big Dill Pickleball Co. launched in 2020 in Salt Lake City as pickleball courts multiplied across church gyms, neighborhood parks, and outdoor courts during the pandemic. Luxem, who grew up in the Pacific Northwest where pickleball was invented, watched the sport surge again and saw a wide gap in the gear being offered to first-time players.

“When I looked at what was available, most of it was clearly built with experienced players in mind,” she said. “I wanted to create something that felt more welcoming for someone walking onto the court for the first time, but that was still high quality and built to last.”

Big Dill Pickleball Co.’s answer was unapologetically playful. Bright colors. Oversized pickles. Starter paddles, sets, and accessories designed for families, cabins, lake houses, and new players who simply wanted to try the game without feeling intimidated. The visual identity made people smile. The high-quality construction made them stay.

That vision took root quickly in the Amazon store, where Big Dill Pickleball Co. launched with a small initial lineup. From the beginning, the business leaned into Amazon’s seller tools to understand how customers were discovering pickleball and what they wanted next.

“We could see what people were searching for and what they were asking for in reviews,” Luxem said. “That data helped us know when to build sets, when to add accessories, and how to talk about the brand.”

A+ Content allowed Big Dill Pickleball Co. to visually tell its story to shoppers, emphasizing that the paddles were playful but built with dependable materials. Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) made fast, reliable shipping possible without Luxem needing to build warehouse infrastructure as demand grew. With FBA, Amazon provides the storage, picking, packing, fulfillment, and customer service for their orders, so Luxem could focus on other parts of her business.

Within three years, the company crossed into seven-figure revenue. Editorial recognition followed, with Big Dill Pickleball Co. appearing in national gift guides and being named one of America’s top small businesses by the US Chamber of Commerce. Even as competition in the category intensified, the Amazon store remains the company’s primary growth engine.

“I tried a lot of different channels,” Luxem said. “But at the end of the day, Amazon is where people are already going when they decide they want to try pickleball. That has always been our core audience.”

While many paddle brands compete for adoption at the highest levels of the sport, Big Dill Pickleball Co. has remained intentionally positioned at the front door of pickleball. Luxem plays three to four times a week herself. Some days are competitive open play. Other nights are casual neighborhood games.

“There is no other sport I would accidentally play for three hours,” she said. “You can play with a 70-year-old one game and a 15-year-old the next. It really is a great equalizer.”

Big Dill Pickleball Co.’s role in the sport’s growth is defined by strengthening the on-ramp to the game itself. The company builds paddles that feel fun and unintimidating to pick up, but that are also durable enough to let players stay on the court long enough to decide if pickleball truly becomes part of their lives.

New players are not learning on disposable gear. They are learning on paddles built to endure hours of play, missed shots, and the trial-and-error that comes with every new sport.

“For the PPA audience, I just want people to remember that recreational players are the foundation of everything,” Luxem said. “That is where the beginners and families are. That is where the future players come from.”

title: Park Place Technologies Announced as Official Technology Partner of Pro Pickleball’s PPA and MLP, Merging Innovation and America’s Fastest-Growing Sport
dek: CLEVELAND, OHIO — Jan. 13, 2025 — Park Place Technologies, a global IT infrastructure services firm based in Cleveland, announced today that it has been named the official technology partner Read more
author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
CLEVELAND, OHIO — Jan. 13, 2025 — Park Place Technologies, a global IT infrastructure services firm based in Cleveland, announced today that it has been named the official technology partner of both the Professional Pickleball Association (Carvana PPA Tour) and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash). 

The sponsorship marks a dynamic partnership between an innovative technology organization and one of the nation’s most exciting emerging sports. As part of this multi-year partnership, Park Place Technologies will become the Official Technology Partner of the PPA Tour and MLP, providing resources for national tournaments, player engagement, fan experiences and educational donations to schools.

“Pickleball’s rapid rise in popularity stems from its ability to unite people through competition, energy and community—the same values that drive innovation at Park Place Technologies,” said Chris Adams, president and CEO of Park Place Technologies. “Our partnership with the Professional Pickleball Association and Major League Pickleball will help to elevate the fan experience and showcase the Park Place brand and culture to this dynamic, growing audience.”

Adams noted that Ohio is one of the top five states in the nation for pickleball courts, with an estimated player base of more than 800,000 and is home to the 2025 MLP Champion Columbus Sliders. The Cleveland area hosts more than 300 courts, including two at Park Place’s global headquarters.

“We’re proud to welcome Park Place Technologies as a key partner in the growth of the PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball,” said Connor Pardoe, CEO of the United Pickleball Association, which operates PPA and MLP. “Its sponsorship will help us amplify the game for fans and players alike.”

The partnership will debut during the 2026 season. Fans can expect to see Park Place’s presence across digital platforms, broadcasts and live events throughout the season.

About Carvana PPA Tour

Founded in 2019, the Carvana PPA Tour is where pickleball’s top athletes go head-to-head to determine the best male and female players in the world. The Carvana PPA Tour organizes and conducts tournaments at world-class facilities across the country, establishes player rankings, and showcases the world’s best pickleball week in and week out. Inviting amateur players to also compete and “play where the pros play,” the Carvana PPA Tour offers divisions for every age group and skill level. Characterized by a uniquely festive and fun atmosphere, Carvana PPA Tour events deliver unparalleled experiences for fans on-site, including pro player meet-and-greets, clinics, food, beverages, live entertainment, giveaways, games, shopping, and VIP upgrades. For more information, go to www.ppatour.com, and follow us on social: Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn.

About Major League Pickleball (MLP Presented By Doordash)

Founded in 2021, Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) is the preeminent, coed, team-based professional pickleball league, featuring over 100 of the best athletes across 23 teams, iconic team owners, and the most electric live events and fan experience in the sport. In 2024, MLP and the PPA Tour merged under the newly-formed United Pickleball Association (UPA), bringing together the leading pro pickleball organizations under a single entity. Visit the official website and follow MLP on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube for more information.

About Park Place Technologies

Park Place Technologies is a leading global IT infrastructure service firm. We help 21,500 organizations – including half the Fortune 500 – fuel innovation by dramatically reducing time and money spent on IT infrastructure management, while boosting performance and uptime. Powered by the world’s largest on-the-ground engineering team, a robust group of advanced engineers, and our global Enterprise Operations Centers, Park Place delivers significant cost savings on hardware maintenance, software technical support, hardware procurement, and more. We also streamline IT infrastructure management, freeing internal teams from day-to-day tasks, enabling them to focus on strategic initiatives.  Park Place Technologies: Save. Simplify. Innovate.  

For more information, visit ParkPlaceTechnologies.com.

author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • GRAND SLAM: Starting the year with a SLAM – worth 2,000 points, double an Open.
  • NATIONAL EYEBALLS: National CBS audience on Sunday at noon Eastern leads into NFL playoffs. 
  • CHOOSE THY WEAPON: Several top players switching paddles – will that affect performance? 
  • HOWELLS AT THE MOON: Will Howells joins the PPA Tour full time – how will he fare in tourney #1?
  • 3 OF A KIND: How many players will claim a title in all 3 disciplines in 2026? Just Anna Leigh Waters, Ben Johns, and Parris Todd hit the trifecta in ’25.

  • Year 4 at Invited’s Mission Hills Country Club.

  • Event #1 in 2026 features a progressive draw, one round per bracket per day.

  • FS1 exclusive window on Saturday from 3:30-5:30 Pacific time. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending medalists: Federico Staksrud, Jaume Martinez Vich, Tyson McGuffin
  • Hunter Johnson is the top seed, entering 2026 as #1, can he win as the favorite?
  • Ben Johns is not playing singles in this event. 
  • Chris Haworth looks to reel in the players at the top of the rankings and wear the #1 crown – he starts 2026 as the 6 seed, after winning in Daytona to close 2025.

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Waters/Johns, Parenteau/Staksrud, Black/Alshon 
  • Jorja and JW Johnson (2) were the clear #2 team in 2025, can they continue that fine play in 2026?
  • Catherine Parenteau and Gabe Tardio (5) pair up to start ‘26, how will they fare? 
  • Howells and Rohrabacher (18) are a dangerous low seed as Howells will have to earn points to improve his seeds across disciplines. 
  • Andrei Daescu is paired with Lacy Schneemann (6) – not Parris Todd as planned who is suspended for this tournament.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • The 3 seed is Alshon/Patriquin – playing for the 3rd time, reached the quarters twice together in ‘24 in Vegas and Kansas City.

  • WATCH OUT FOR: Daescu and Staksrud (2) – “right side Fed” won with Patriquin at Nationals, now he pairs with Daescu in the other half of the 2 and 3 seed mashup. This is their first tournament together.

title: Before Anna Leigh Waters: A Look at Pickleball’s Earlier Benchmarks
dek: Have you ever wondered what some of the -old- records were before Anna Leigh Waters obliterated them? Like in Baseball… Roger Connor finished his career with 138 home runs, then Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Have you ever wondered what some of the -old- records were before Anna Leigh Waters obliterated them?  Like in Baseball… Roger Connor finished his career with 138 home runs, then Babe Ruth blew by him and went up to 714. Here’s a quick look at the progression of some Women’s PPA historical records:

SINGLES: 
  • Simone Jardim had six titles, all in 2020 and 2021.
  • Waters earned her seventh at the National Indoor Championships in February 2022. Waters enters 2026 with 57 Singles titles.
DOUBLES:
  • Simone Jardim had 14 titles through the Texas Open in September 2021.
  • Lucy Kovalova passed Jardim with her 15th title at the Arizona Slam in February 2022, and ran her total up to 21 at Newport Beach in April 2023. 
  • Waters earned her record-breaking 22nd title at the Takeya Showcase in August 2023. She enters 2026 with 56 Women’s Doubles titles.
MIXED DOUBLES:
  • Simone Jardim earned her 12th and final Mixed Doubles title at the Rocky Mountain Championships in August 2021.
  • Waters passed Jardim with her 13th title at the Hertz National Championships in December 2022. She enters 2026 with 59 Mixed Doubles titles.

The previous records were 6, 21 and 12 before Waters passed them and ran her totals into the 50s in all three categories, and of course, she’s not done yet. A “Ruthian” feat, for sure.

*** Ben Johns has been #1 in all three categories since Day One. However, in Men’s Doubles he was briefly tied at two and again at three before he stayed ahead for good with his fourth title at the Arizona Slam in February 2021.

  • 6, Catherine Parenteau. (1 S, 5 D)
  • 5, Federico Staksrud. (4 S, 1 D)
Fundamentals

Players in a Doubles final who did not hit a ball “out” on a serve, return, third shot, or dink:

  • CJ Klinger, Atlanta Slam, Men’s Doubles. 
  • Anna Leigh Waters, Atlanta Slam, Women’s Doubles.
  • Andrei Daescu, Cincinnati Open, Men’s Doubles.
Blunt Force Trauma

Doubles finals where every rally was fewer than 30 shots, and 65% or more of the rallies were nine shots or fewer: 

  • Daescu/Johns def. Alshon/Staksrud, Cape Coral Open, 11-2, 11-7, 11-1.
  • Johns/Tardio def. Martinez Vich/Wright, Bristol Open, 11-1, 11-6, 11-2.
Sweet “Pickles”

There were two 11-0 games in finals in 2025: 

  • Masters, Women’s Singles. (Waters vs Christian, Game One)
  • Tucson Open, Women’s Doubles. (Parenteau/Waters vs Bright/Rohrabacher, Game One)
Clean Winners

Players with 20-or-more Clean Winners in a final (no net or opponent’s paddle):

  • 33, Dekel Bar, Red Rock Open, Mixed Doubles. (Mixed Doubles record)
  • 31, Kaitlyn Christian, Vegas Open, Singles. (Women’s Singles record)
  • 28, Christian Alshon, Red Rock Open, Mixed Doubles.
  • 24, Connor Garnett, Atlanta Slam, Singles.
  • 23, Ben Johns, Atlanta Slam, Singles.
  • 22, Anna Leigh Waters, Atlanta Slam, Singles.
  • 22, Kate Fahey, Cincinnati Open, Singles.
  • 20. Gabe Tardio, Australian Open, Singles.
  • 20, Kaitlyn Christian, Australian Open, Singles.
  • 20, Christian Alshon, Texas Open, Singles.
  • 20, Kaitlyn Christian, Bristol Open, Singles.
Raising the Bar

Dekel Bar’s 33 Clean Winners and 14 Ernes in the Mixed Doubles final at the Red Rock Open were both the most in a Gender Doubles or Mixed Doubles final since the start of 2022.  

Breakthrough

Jade Kawamoto became the first left-handed female player ever to win a title. She won the Women’s Doubles title in Cincinnati with her sister Jackie. CJ Klinger and Augie Ge are the only other left-handers to win championships.

Longest Rally in a Final

100 shots, Lakeland Open. Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns won the rally, and the match, against Jorja and JW Johnson. 

Undefeated 

Anna Leigh Waters had her first undefeated calendar year in Singles. She won all twelve of the tournaments that she entered. Her only other undefeated calendar year was in 2023, in Doubles.

title: The ABC’s of 2025
dek: *Anna Leigh and Ben’s Championships in calendar year 2025) (all stats cited refer to gold medal matches) ANNA LEIGH WATERS: Medals: Waters won 38 gold medals, two silver medals, and Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
*Anna Leigh and Ben’s Championships in calendar year 2025)

(all stats cited refer to gold medal matches)

ANNA LEIGH WATERS:

Medals: Waters won 38 gold medals, two silver medals, and three bronze medals in 17 tournaments.  She had only one tournament where she did not win at least one gold medal.

Singles: Waters won 12 times in 12 tournaments, the first time she has gone undefeated in a calendar year in Singles. 

   In 12 gold medal matches, Waters won 24 games while losing only two games. Brooke Buckner led 11-4 and 9-4 at Mesa, and Fahey won a game 11-7 at Atlanta. Fahey played her especially closely, losing games by the scores of 15-13, 13-11 and 12-10. 

   Waters held her opponents to seven points or fewer in a finals game 19 times. Waters had more “Clean Winners” than her opponent in ten of those twelve finals. She beat eight different players in those gold medal matches, and won her 50th career Singles title at Red Rock.

Doubles: Waters won 13 golds, one silver and two bronze medals in 17 tournaments. 

   Waters and Catherine Parenteau won five golds and one silver medal. In their six finals, they lost six of 22 games, with three of those at the hands of Tyra Black at Jorja Johnson at North Carolina…the only time Waters lost back-to-back games all year.

   Waters and Anna Bright won seven golds and two bronzes. In their seven finals, they lost only one of 22 games (to Tyra Black and Parris Todd at Worlds). Black was the only player to win a game in a final against both Waters/Parenteau and Waters/Bright. In Waters/Bright’s recent streak of four consecutive wins from Virginia Beach to Lakeland, Waters had the most “Clean Winners” in those gold medal matches all four times.

   Waters finished 2025 with a title at Daytona Beach with Jorja Johnson. Oh by the way, Waters also finished 2024 by winning at Daytona Beach with her mother, Leigh Waters.

Mixed Doubles: Waters and Ben Johns won 13 golds, one silver and one bronze medal in 15 tournaments. They medaled in every tournament in which they played. Their silver medal was against the Johnsons in North Carolina, and they earned a bronze medal in Mesa after losing to Anna Bright and Dekel Bar in the semis.

   Waters and Johns lost only eleven games in 14 finals. JW Johnson was on the other side of the net for nine of those eleven games. JW and his sister Jorja played Waters/Bright exceptionally well, beating them once and losing in five games twice. The only time all year that Waters and Johns lost back-to-back games  was to the Johnsons.

   Eight of Waters/Johns’ victories came in three straight games, including four tournaments in a row from Cincinnati to the Words. Their win at Orange County was their 50th together.

Triple Crowns: Waters earned eight Triple Crowns, raising her career and PPA-record total to 39. She won four consecutive Triple Crowns from Virginia Beach to Lakeland, the fourth time she has won Triple Crowns in four or more consecutive tournaments.

Greatness on Gold Medal Games: Waters won 84% of the games she played in gold medal matches, compiling a record of 105-20. When she or her team won the first game, she had a record of 32-2, and a 6-0 mark when her opponent won the first game.

2026: Waters enters the new year with 172 titles: 57 Singles, 56 Doubles, and 59 Mixed Doubles. Her “lowest” total, 56 in Doubles, is still more than the overall career titles won by any other player other than Ben Johns. Her longest active winning streak in tournaments played is 19 in Singles, dating back to June 2024.

BEN JOHNS: 

Medals: Johns won 26 gold medals, three silvers and two bronzes in 15 tournaments.

Singles: Johns won titles in Mesa (against Hunter Johnson) and Atlanta (against Connor Garnett), but had no other medal-winning outings. He was eliminated prior to the semifinals six times.

Doubles: Johns won eleven golds, two silvers, and one bronze. He won one gold with Collin Johns, one gold with Andrei Daescu, and one bronze with Hayden Patriquin. Playing with Gabe Tardio since March, they won nine golds and two silvers together in twelve tournaments.

   It took a while for Johns and Tardio to gel as a team. In their first five tournaments together, they won three golds and two silvers, and won eleven of 22 games in the finals. In their seven tournaments since then (starting with Bristol), they have six golds and a fourth place. They won 18 of 21 games in their six finals, a marked improvement from the eleven of 22 they won in the first half of the year.

   In their first final together in Mesa, Johns and Tardio lost to Christian Alshon and Andrei Daescu, then beat them in the four finals they faced them after that.

Mixed Doubles: Johns and Anna Leigh Waters dominated again, winning 13 of the 19 gold medals offered this year. Eight of those 13 wins were three-game sweeps, including four of their last five. Johns and Waters did not play (or play together) in four events, and had one silver medal and one bronze. The Johnsons claimed four of the other six titles.

Triple Crowns: Johns did not have a Triple Crown this year for the first time. He played in all three finals only once, in Atlanta. He has 21 career Triple Crowns.

Greatness on Gold Medal Games: Johns won 75% of the games he played in gold medal matches, compiling a record of 80-26. When Johns or his team won the first game of a gold medal match, he had a record of 20-1, the only blemish being a loss in Mixed Doubles. He was 6-2 when his opponent won the first game.

2026: Johns enters the new year with 169 titles: 42 Singles, 55 Doubles, and 72 Mixed Doubles. His “lowest” total, 42 in Singles, is still more than the overall career titles won by any other player other than Waters and Parenteau. His longest active winning streak in tournaments played is nine in Mixed Doubles, dating back to North Carolina in April.  

Johns is the only player to have won at least one gold medal in every year since the Tour’s inception in 2020.

title: Carvana Named Title Sponsor of The PPA Masters, One of Pickleball’s Most Prestigious Tournaments
dek: Carvana (NYSE: CVNA), an industry pioneer for buying and selling cars online, today announced it will become the title sponsor of The PPA Masters tournament, one of the PPA Tour’s Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
Carvana (NYSE: CVNA), an industry pioneer for buying and selling cars online, today announced it will become the title sponsor of The PPA Masters tournament, one of the PPA Tour’s largest Slam events. The tournament will be renamed The Carvana Masters, further strengthening the company’s long-standing commitment to pickleball fans, players, and the sport’s continued growth.

The Carvana Masters is scheduled for Jan. 12-18, 2026, at Mission Hills Country Club in Rancho Mirage, California.

As title sponsor, Carvana will help elevate both the fan and player experience at one of pickleball’s premier tournaments. This year’s event will feature an expanded on-site Carvana presence, including the popular Dink It Challenge, and prize opportunities for fans.

The Carvana Masters will bring together top pros, rising talent, and passionate fans for a week of world-class competition, community, and celebration. Featuring the iconic tradition of players wearing all-white, set against the backdrop of pristine green courts, The Carvana Masters will kick off 2026 in style. The event is scheduled for Jan. 12-18, 2026, at Mission Hills Country Club in Rancho Mirage, California.

For more information, please visit www.carvana.com.

title: My time at the PPA Tour Cincinnati Open Tournament
dek: Erica Schiebel – Global Consumer Experience Manager, FUTURO™ Brand “I had no idea what I was in for attending my first pickleball tournament. Sure, I had heard of how in Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Erica Schiebel – Global Consumer Experience Manager, FUTURO™ Brand

“I had no idea what I was in for attending my first pickleball tournament. Sure, I had heard of how in the US the sport of pickleball was sweeping the nation and getting so huge in popularity a whole new industry of sporting goods was growing, businesses were popping up for outdoor and indoor play, and even old-school neighborhood tennis courts were being repurposed to pickleball courts. It had gotten so big, one of the brands I support at 3M, FUTURO™ Brand, had actually decided to become a sponsor of the Professional Pickleball Association’s Tour.

The setup day for the Cincinnati Open was pretty quiet, and my coworker and I got our activation space ready. We were positioned right near the championship courts, and a few folks were passing by starting the early tournament play and getting the center ready to go for the rest of the event.

As we got started the next day at the official start of the tournament, the traffic to our booth increased. It ebbed and flowed between matches and as play got going. We had all ages, genders, backgrounds stop by with interesting stories. People from all parts of the US from Illinois, to California and Arizona to Florida and New Jersey. We even had Canadians too! Through the week we spoke to parents looking for solutions for their kid players as young as 8 to players who were still going strong and playing on a regular basis in their 80s. Their stamina and athleticism was so impressive! A few folks shared they travel the circuit and go from tournament to tournament. It sounds like a wonderful life to travel and play a sport you love at the same time. 

What stood out to me is how happy and friendly everyone was. Everyone that stopped by our vendor booth was cheerful and courteous and in a good mood. Even those that lost matches bubbled with kindness and enthusiasm. And like smiles and laughter could be contagious, the positive energy was flowing, and we were catching in on the positivity. 

Our purpose at the event was to introduce our FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves for knee, elbow and ankle that came out this spring. These sleeves help support your joints and help provide relief where you need it. With active pickleball athletes we were able to fit quite a few with samples to help them keep moving on the court, or even find some relief to make it home or back to the hotel comfortably after a hard day of play. 

One of the most rewarding parts of the activation was seeing the comfort and relief on people’s faces when they got on our compression sleeves on. In some cases we even heard an “Oh” or an “Ah”. It felt so good being able to help people that were in pain or had discomfort.

This event really opened my eyes to the magic of pickleball. With what I thought would be a long week leaving me tired and exhausted, I actually came home happy and energized, and, ready to pick up a paddle.”

Check us out on futuro-usa.com/compression

title: Storylines for the Florida Dairy Farmers Daytona Beach Open
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • DO YOU HEAR WHAT I HEAR?: In 2024, CJ Klinger won his first title in Daytona in men’s doubles (with Daescu). Will another player grab his/her first title here in ’25?
  • IT’S THE MOST WONDERFUL TIME OF THE YEAR: Can Kaitlyn Christian and Federico Staksrud defend their singles titles? 
  • 3 FRENCH HENS?: Just a partridge in a pear tree possibility for Anna Leigh Waters as she is only playing women’s doubles (with Jorja Johnson!).  
  • WINTER WONDERLAND? Uh…no. Perfect pickleball weather with highs in the low 70s expected. 
  • OPEN THOSE PRESENTS: 1000 points to the winners. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Tourney #20 on the campaign – playing at Pictona in Holly Hill.  
  • Over 1,200 players participating across all divisions. 
  • Semi-Final Saturday Open Format: singles Wednesday, mixed Thursday, men’s/women’s doubles Friday – all through the quarters, Semifinal Saturday, and Championship Sunday.  
  • PickleballTV (and the app) will have the coverage, starting at 11am Eastern on Wednesday-Friday, 10am Eastern Saturday and Sunday. Tennis Channel coverage 3-6pm Eastern Thursday through Saturday and 2-5pm Eastern on Championship Sunday. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending medalists: Kaitlyn Christian, Dom Schaefer, Mary Brascia
  • Anna Leigh Waters is not in the singles draw (playing women’s only) so she will end the 2025 campaign a perfect 59-0 in singles. 
  • Kate Fahey and Brooke Buckner also taking this tournament off. 
  • Christian is the top seed, Lea Jansen is the (2). 
  • Good potential quarterfinal matchup: Genie Bouchard (4) vs. Judit Castillo (6)
  • Watch out for: Catherine Parenteau. Hasn’t won a singles gold since August of ’23 – is this her week?  

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending medalists: Federico Staksrud, Zane Ford, Michael Loyd
  • Staksrud is back as #1 in the world, is the top seed, and the defending champion. 
  • Hunter Johnson, Roscoe Bellamy, and Jack Sock are not in the tournament. 
  • Twoeys for days in a potential quarterfinal between Connor Garnett (5) and Gabe Joseph (3).
  • Watch out for: John Lucian Goins (6) – can he find his top form that propelled him to back to back wins this summer? 

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Jorja Johnson/Hayden Patriquin, Tina Pisnik/Andrei Daescu, Anna Bright/Dekel Bar
  • No GOATS – Waters (just playing women’s) and Ben Johns (out of the tournament)
  • Johnsons are the top seed, looking for their 4th mixed win in 2025. 
  • Christian Alshon and Tyra Black are the 2 seed and both continue to seek their 1st mixed gold. 
  • Watch out for: Irvine/Tardio (3) – last tourney together for the foreseeable future as Tardio will play with Catherine Parenteau in 2026. 

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Waters/Waters, Johnson/Black, Bright/Jackie Kawamoto
  • Anna Leigh Waters and Jorja Johnson are paired up for the 1st time as the 1 seed. 
  • Anna Bright is not playing in the tournament. 
  • Potential Utah dominant fun quarterfinal: Rohrabacher/Tuionetoa (3) vs. Allyce Jones/Callie Smith (5)
  • Watch out for: First time partners Parenteau and Black – can they make a run to Sunday as the 2 seed?

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Andrei Daescu/CJ Klinger, Dekel Bar/Pablo Tellez, Hayden Patriquin/Federico Staksrud
  • Daescu/Tardio are the top seed – this pair won twice in 2024.  
  • FLASH MOB ALERT: JW Johnson and Augie Ge (3) are playing their first Carvana PPA tour event together – members of the 2024 MLP champions, the Dallas Flash. 
  • Must see potential round of 16 matchup: AJ Koller/Connor Garnett (9) vs. Dekel Bar/Pablo Tellez (6) 
  • Watch out for: Tom Protzek/Jay Devilliers (8) – Protzek with a chance as a high seed to make a run with “Team Europe” (Protzek from Germany, Devilliers from France).

title: Proton paddles, including new Project Peacock, now available at DICK’S Sporting Goods and Scheels
dek: Starting on Wednesday, Proton pickleball paddles are available in-store and online at both DICK’S Sporting Goods and Scheels, marking a major milestone in Proton’s meteoric rise in popularity in just Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Starting on Wednesday, Proton pickleball paddles are available in-store and online at both DICK’S Sporting Goods and Scheels, marking a major milestone in Proton’s meteoric rise in popularity in just under two years.

Landing distribution with DICK’S alone is considered one of the most competitive achievements in the sporting goods industry. With hundreds of brands vying for limited shelf space, only a select group earns placement through DICK’S rigorous product evaluation process, one that requires exceptional performance, durability, and customer demand. Proton now joins that elite roster, while simultaneously launching in Scheels Sporting Goods, which is a feat in and of itself.

Proton has gone from a little-known startup, to one of the most exciting and innovative paddle makers in the sport since debuting their first paddles to the market in July 2024. Their focus on engineering, durability, and flashy paddle designs has earned both national and international attention, in large part due to the wildly popular Series Three Project Flamingo Paddle, which has become a favorite among pro players and amateurs alike. The Flamingo, available in both an elongated and square shape in 13mm and 15mm thicknesses, is one of the reasons why DICK’S and Scheels approached Proton.

Alongside the dual-retail rollout, Proton is unveiling its newest model in the acclaimed Series Three family: The Project Peacock. Designed for players who want to stand out, the Peacock blends vibrant style with Proton’s most advanced technology to date.

The Project Peacock features Proton’s high-density Atomic Foam Core, offering lightweight stability, enhanced feel, and longer dwell time—without sacrificing power. Built with aerospace-grade materials, the paddle is engineered to eliminate issues like delamination and core crush, giving players unmatched confidence shot after shot. In fact, in independent evaluations, the Peacock underwent extensive durability testing and maintained solid performance over thousands of hits. The Peacock’s roughness-enhanced surface also delivers maximum allowable spin, helping players shape shots with laser precision.

With dual certifications from UPA-A and USAP, the Project Peacock is tournament-ready.

“We’re thrilled to share that players can now find Proton paddles, including our brand-new Project Peacock paddle, at both DICK’S Sporting Goods AND Scheels. This represents a significant accomplishment for our team and a proud moment for our community,” said Charles Darling, the founder of Proton Pickleball. “DICK’S and Scheels are two of the most respected and trusted retailers in the sporting world, and partnering with them both allows us to bring Proton’s innovation and craftsmanship to even more players nationwide. We couldn’t be more excited for what’s ahead.”

Specifications for Project Peacock paddle (Elongated 15mm)

Overall Length: 16.5 inches
Overall Width: 7.5 inches
Thickness: 15mm
Average Weight: 8.0 oz
Grip Circumference: 4.25 inches
Handle Length: 5.375 inches
Core: Proprietary high-density Atomic Foam Core
Surface: Roughness-enhanced raw carbon fiber

title: 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships Break Attendance, Participation, and Viewership Records
dek: The 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships returned to Brookhaven Country Club in Farmers Branch, Texas, and smashed records. A crowd of 60,000+, bringing in more than $1.1 million in Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
The 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships returned to Brookhaven Country Club in Farmers Branch, Texas, and smashed records. A crowd of 60,000+, bringing in more than $1.1 million in combined ticket and hospitality revenue, were on hand to witness pickleball’s greatest player, 18-year-old Anna Leigh Waters, become the winningest player in Carvana PPA Tour history, achieving a remarkable triple crown victory to win her record-breaking 168th career title.

Nearly all 50 states were represented in the amateur competition ranks, which saw a record 4,400 total participants, including players from 38 countries competing in more than 6,000 matches throughout the week in what is truly the world’s greatest pickleball event. 

Fan engagement was equally extraordinary. Pickleballtv saw a record 70 million minutes viewed across the event and official social media handles reached rarified air, accumulating 54 million impressions. Earned media coverage also generated a record-setting 1.2 billion potential international and domestic impressions (+50% vs. last year’s event). 

“We came back to Brookhaven this year in anticipation of putting on the largest, greatest event the pickleball world has ever known, and we did just that,” said Carvana PPA Tour Founder & CEO Connor Pardoe. “This was the 100th PPA event and it was a remarkable showcase of how much we have grown, with intense competition on both the pro and amateur side, and the insane crowds filling Pickleball Boulevard and Nature’s Sunshine Championship Court daily. We feel confident in saying that the 2025 edition of the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships was the most extraordinary tournament in pro pickleball history.”

“Being at the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships was electric,” said Jenius Bank President John Rosenfeld. “The energy on the grounds, the level of competition, and the passion of this community are unmatched. We’re proud to champion a sport that brings people together and celebrates what it means to live richer lives—on and off the court.”

The event, which spanned two weekends, beginning with the Edward Jones MLP Cup from October 31 – Nov. 2, saw the largest amalgamation of pickleball ever seen. The St. Louis Shock, featuring star players Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin, took home the MLP Cup, defeating the hometown Dallas Flash in an epic battle of MLP juggernauts. Alongside the MLP Cup on the first weekend was the first-ever Adidas Collegiate World Championships, which saw teams from universities across the world gather to compete for the title of collegiate world champion, a title which Utah Tech University now claims.

As the week progressed, the pickleball celebration continued, seeing incredible competition from the Junior PPA players, along with the adaptive wheelchair competition, and the Battle of the Badges and Battle of the Branches, which saw military veterans and first responders duke it out on the courts. Wednesday night’s Celebrity Pickleball Showdown was a huge hit, seeing NBA Hall of Famer Dirk Nowitzki, World Series Champion J.D. Martinez, NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens and international gaming star Tfue go paddle-to-paddle with pro pickleball’s best, including Waters, Ben Johns, and Bright. The final weekend also bore witness to the PPA Challenger Showdown, in which the top players from this year’s inaugural PPA Challenger Series season competed for their pickleball dream, a Carvana PPA Tour contract offer. 

From the record-setting crowds witnessing pickleball’s biggest star achieve a milestone victory at the Carvana PPA Tour’s centennial event, to an astounding national and international turnout of amateur and collegiate players, unmatched programming events and competitions, and incredible concerts on the FLIGHT by Yuengling Stage, the 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships was a tournament that set the bar for what professional pickleball can be.

dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • 101: The next hundred tournaments starts in Lakeland. 
  • QUADRUPLE TRIPLE: Can Anna Leigh Waters win her 4th triple crown in a row?
  • ABCDEFGIJKL: What’s missing? H. Patriquin is taking time off after winning Worlds.
  • HUNTED/HUNTER: Hunter Johnson falls back to spot #2 in the singles rankings – how will he fare?
  • OPEN IT UP: 1000 points to the winners. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Tourney #19 on the campaign – playing at the Beerman Family Tennis Center which is 45 minutes from Walt Disney World to the east and 49 minutes to Busch Gardens to the west. 
  • Over 800 players participating across all divisions. 
  • Semi-Final Saturday Open Format: singles Wednesday, mixed Thursday, men’s/women’s doubles Friday – all through the quarters, Semifinal Saturday, and Championship Sunday.  
  • PickleballTV (and the app) will have the coverage, starting at 11am Eastern on Wednesday-Friday, 10am Eastern Saturday and Sunday. Tennis Channel coverage 12-4 Eastern Saturday. 
  • No defending medalists. 

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Will Waters’ undefeated 2025 campaign continue in her home state?
  • Devidze (15), the last player to beat Waters in May ’24, could face her again in the R16. 
  • Kaitlyn Christian will not get another shot at Waters after their classic Worlds battle as she is not in the draw. 
  • Watch out for: Kate Fahey. She has solidified herself at the #2 spot and pushed Waters in the Worlds final – could face Jansen (5) in the quarterfinals.   

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Staksrud (1) is back on top after winning Worlds – can he stay there? 
  • Ben Johns has slipped to the 8 seed and would face Staksrud in the quarters if seeds hold. 
  • Must see R16 potential matchup: Sock (7) vs. Florida resident Goins (9). 
  • Watch out for: Chris Haworth (6) – has climbed from 57th to the 6th seed in short order and played well at Worlds before falling to Staksrud in the final.

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Waters/Johns (1) have won 8 straight tourneys they have entered – will this be #9?
  • Fun R32 matchup: Fahey/Frazier (10) vs. Devilliers/Jackie Kawamoto (17)
  • Oncins and Bright (4) – pair up for the first time, looking to medal.  
  • Biggest age discrepancy EVER in the PPA and thanks for the memories: Steve Deakin, 51 years of age, pairs with Elsie Hendershot (12 years old) in Deakin’s last ever pro tournament. 
  • Watch out for: Black/Alshon (3) – neither player has won a gold in mixed on the Carvana PPA Tour.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • They’re baaack. “Wonder twin powers activate” – Kawamotos (5) hit the court together for the first time since winning the Cincinnati Slam in September. 
  • Waters and Bright (1) look to win 4 tourneys in a row. 
  • Rachel Rohrabacher is paired with Jorja Johnson as the 3 seed – how healthy will she be after the injury she suffered in the semis at Worlds?
  • Watch out for: Parenteau and Tuionetoa – playing together for the first time as the 4 seed.    

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Johns/Tardio (1) missed getting to Championship Sunday for the first time ever at Worlds.  
  • Right side Staksrud will have to wait to go back over there as he will most likely play left with McGuffin as a first-time partnership and the 4 seed. 
  • JW Johnson/CJ Klinger (3) – made an impressive run to the Worlds final, including a win over Team Power Forward Daescu/Alshon (2).   
  • Watch out for: Martinez Vich/Devilliers (6) – this showtime team could do serious damage in their debut together.

author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Farmers Branch, Texas

November 9, 2025

.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL:  Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (2) Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson, 11-7, 11-4, 11-7.

  • Waters and Johns: 12th title this year, and 56th together. (Overall: Waters 58, Johns 71)
  • The Johnsons beat Waters and Johns in the gold medal match in North Carolina in April.
  • Waters and Johns had more Clean Winners (20-14).

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL:  (3) Hayden Patriquin and Federico Staksrud def. (4) JW Johnson and CJ Klinger, 8-11, 11-7, 11-4, 11-8.

  • Patriquin and Staksrud: 4th title together. (Overall: Patriquin 5, Staksrud 6)
  • Patriquin has won back-to-back Men’s Doubles titles at Worlds (2024, Newman)
  • Johnson had more errors on Serves-Returns-Thirds than Patriquin and Staksrud, (11-8).
  • Klinger had more volleys onto the net than Patriquin and Staksrud, (17-16).
  • Longest rally: 75 shots (final rally of the match).

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL:  (1) Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Catherine Parenteau and Parris Todd, 11-2, 11-2, 11-5.

  • Bright and Waters: 6th title this year, and 13th together. (Overall: Bright 22, Waters 54)
  • Bright’s 22nd Women’s Doubles title broke a tie with Lucy Kovalova for third most all-time.
  • Bright and Waters had more Clean Winners (20-6).
  • Bright had no errors on Serves-Return-Thirds.
  • Waters had no Dinks into the net or wide.
  • Longest rally: 56 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (2) Federico Staksrud def. (13) Christopher Haworth, 11-9, 11-1.

  • Staksrud has won three of the last four tournaments.
  • Staksrud’s 17 titles are second-most all-time behind Ben Johns (42).
  • Staksrud has fewer Serve and Return Errors (7-1).
  • Staksrud had fewer Baseline Drive Errors (13-3).
  • Staksrud trailed in Game One 5-0, then outscored Haworth 22-5.
  • Longest rally: 12 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL:  (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Kate Fahey, 11-4, 12-10.

  • Waters’s 11th title this year and 56th overall.
  • Waters has won 45 consecutive Finals appearances.
  • Part of Waters’ 38th career Triple Crown, and 168th overall title, breaking a tie with Ben Johns.
  • Waters had more Clean Winners (13-5).
  • Longest rally: 13 shots.

.
