title: Storylines for the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships – November 3-9, 2025
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • CENTURY MARK: This is the 100th tournament in the PPA Tour’s history — going from 2,000 fans in Mesa in 2020 to over 55,000+ expected at Worlds this year.  
  • TITLES: Ben Johns has 166 career gold medals — Anna Leigh Waters is just one behind at 165.  
  • STREAKS: Waters in undefeated in singles in 2025 and Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio look to win their 7th men’s doubles title in a row as a team. 
  • 3 GRAND: 3,000 points on the line – two times a Cup and 3X an Open – one good week could catapult a player up the rankings. 
  • BIG D(IRK): Dallas Maverick’s Hall of Famer Dirk Nowitzki headlines the Wednesday night celebrity pro-am – 7pm Central start. 

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Tourney #18 on the campaign – return to Invited’s Brookhaven Country Club in Farmers Branch, Texas (suburb of Dallas).  
  • Over 3,500 players participating across all divisions. 
  • Progressive Format: Round of 64 Tuesday, Round of 32 Wednesday, Round of 16 Thursday, Quarterfinal Friday, Semifinal Saturday, and Championship Sunday.  
  • PickleballTV (and the app) will have the coverage, starting each day at 10am Central, with Tennis Channel coverage on Wednesday and Saturday.

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Anna Leigh Waters, Kate Fahey, Salome Devidze
  • Anna Leigh Waters (1) hasn’t lost a singles match in over 500 days – could have an early battle with Jorja Johnson (15) in the round of 16. 
  • Fahey (2) would face Parenteau (7) in the quarters if seeds hold. 
  • Lea Jansen (5), who won the LT Open singles only title, could face Devidze (12) the defending bronze medalist in the round of 16. 
  • Watch out for: Genie Bouchard (9) – made her second final in Las Vegas, beating Parenteau and Fahey on her run to silver.

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Federico Staksrud, Michael Loyd, Hunter Johnson
  • Staksrud (2) is riding the momentum of a win in Vegas last week where he had to save match points against vs. Sock (6). 
  • Marshall Brown (17) soaring into Worlds after a run to the semis in Las Vegas. 
  • Roscoe Bellamy made a great run to the final in Vegas – he is the (11) and would face Jaume Martinez Vich (5) in the quarters if both players make it to that round. 
  • Watch out for: Ben Johns (7) – with 3,000 points on the line, will the GOAT with the 7 seed by his name make a run to the final?

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Anna Leigh Waters/Ben Johns, Etta Tuionetoa/Christian Alshon, Rohrabacher/Staksrud
  • Gabe Tardio/Jessie Irvine (5) – played brilliantly in Vegas on a run to the silver medal and look to carry that over in Texas. 
  • Fun R32 matchup: Kovalova/Wright (25) vs. Stratman/ Donald Young (40). 
  • Double southpaws – Jade Kawamoto is paired with Augie Ge (22) – lefty/lefty is a rare pairing. 
  • Bar and Parenteau (7) last played together in 2021. 
  • Watch out for: Rohrabacher/Daescu (6) – won game 1 before falling 11-9 in the 3rd to Waters and Johns in the quarters in Vegas.  

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Rohrabacher/Bright, Waters/Parenteau, Black/Jones
  • Waters and Bright (1) look to win 3 tourneys in a row. 
  • Parenteau is back with Todd as the 2 seed. They made the final in the Vegas on the Strip event, losing to Johnson and Black. 
  • Rohrabacher/Jade Kawamoto, first time partners, are the 4 seed and the perfect righty/lefty blend that could run it all the way to Sunday. 
  • Watch out for: Johnson and Black (3) – beat Waters/Bright earlier this year and will have the Dallas Flash mob behind them.

  • Defending medalists: Newman/Patriquin, Bar/Tellez, Staksrud/Wright
  • Johns/Tardio (1) beat Alshon/Daescu (2) 12-10 in the fifth in the Vegas final last week in the longest match in Carvana PPA Tour history – 2 hours and 28 minutes. 
  • Wright and Oncins (5) run it back and look to get to the semis or farther again as a pair. 
  • Defending champion Riley Newman (with Patriquin) is paired with Jay Devilliers this year as the 6 seed.  
  • Watch out for: JW Johnson/CJ Klinger (4) – the team known as Ice/Ice for their calm on court demeanor is the last team to beat Johns/Tardio – in Atlanta in May.

title: “Best Match Ever,” a Top Ten List.
dek: The Men’s Doubles Final from the Rate Vegas Cup has been called the “Best Match Ever.” Here are some of the notable highlights: Those are some serious qualifications. What about Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
The Men’s Doubles Final from the Rate Vegas Cup has been called the “Best Match Ever.”  Here are some of the notable highlights:
  • Highest score in a Men’s Doubles Final Game Five since April 2023 (13-11 at Red Rock).
  • Most combined points scored in a Men’s Doubles Final since May 2022. (99 points at Atlanta).
  • Alshon and Daescu had a Game Point in one game and Match Point in another, but won neither game and lost the match. This had never happened in any PPA final, since at least the start of 2022. 

Those are some serious qualifications. What about some other “best ever” matches? There have certainly been several outstanding early round matches, and even some great four-game finals, but since this was a five-game final, let’s go “apples to apples.”  Here are nine more matches to fill out a “Top Ten outstanding/memorable five-game finals in PPA history,” (Since the start of 2022 and in reverse chronological order): 

2025 Red Rock Open, Mixed Doubles:  Parris Todd and Dekel Bar def. Catherine Parenteau and Christian Alshon, 11-9, 12-14, 6-11, 11-7, 11-8. Many will remember this as the “Dekel Bar Match.” He set records with 33 Clean Winners and 14 Ernes, both being the most in any PPA final since at least the start of 2022.

2025 Australia Open, Mixed Doubles: Lacy Schneemann and Tyson McGuffin def. Jessie Irvine and Gabe Tardio, 8-11, 6-11, 11-9, 11-8 11-8. Schneeman and McGuffin were two points away from being swept, down 9-6-1 in Game Three.

2024 Milwaukee Open, Women’s Doubles: Anna Bright and Rachel Rohrabacher def. Jackie Kawamoto and Jade Kawamoto, 4-11, 11-6, 11-7, 10-12, 11-7. Bright and Rohrabacher had a Match Point in Game Four but lost that game, then trailed 5-2 in Game Five. Despite the Kawamotos seeming to have momentum, Bright and Rohrabacher rallied back. This was a deliberately-played match: two-thirds of the rallies were ten shots or more, and the match averaged 17.9 shots per rally.

2024 Las Vegas Cup, Women’s Doubles: Catherine Parenteau and Anna Leigh Waters def. Anna Bright and Rachel Rohrabacher, 10-12, 11-9, 6-11, 11-6, 12-10.  “The Girlies” winning Game One 12-10 set the tone for this rollercoaster. Bright and Rohrabacher led 6-2 in Game Five, and had a Match Point at 10-9-2. Parenteau and Waters were pushed to the brink.

2024 Kansas City Open, Mixed Doubles: Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson, 11-2, 10-12, 12-10, 6-11, 11-2. This was the first final where Waters and Johns were pushed to five games. The Johnsons had two Game Points in Game Three to take a 2-1 lead, but could not convert. Johns has 21 Clean Winners, JW had 20, a rare 20-20 combination.

2023 PPA Championships (Las Vegas), Men’s Doubles: Ben Johns and Collin Johns def. Dylan Frazier and JW Johnson, 7-11, 3-11, 11-7, 11-8, 11-6. Frazier and Johnson were serving 6-6-1 in Game Three with a chance to sweep the Johns brothers, but Ben and Collin put together a massive comeback.

2023 Tournament of Champions (Brigham City, Utah), Men’s Doubles: James Ignatowich and Tyson McGuffin def. AJ Koller and Riley Newman, 5-11, 4-11, 11-0, 11-7, 11-8. Notable for the Game Three turnaround, a twelve-rally first-server “pickle.” All four players had at least ten Clean Winners, and this was part of McGuffin’s Triple Crown. 

2023 Red Rock Open, Men’s Doubles: Brendon Long and Tyson McGuffin def. Dekel Bar and Collin Johns, 11-1, 3-11, 8-11, 11-8, 13-11. Long and McGuffin fended off Match Points at 10-7-2 and 11-10-2 in that 13-11 Game Five. 

2022 Red Rock Open, Men’s Doubles: Ben Johns and Collin Johns def. AJ Koller and Riley Newman, 11-4, 11-8, 6-11, 9-11, 11-8. The Johns brothers rallied back from an 8-3-2 deficit in Game Five.

title: 5 Recovery Items for Sprains, Strains, Swelling, Soreness, and Stiffness
dek: If you’ve ever dealt with a twisted ankle, sore knee, or that all-too-familiar tennis elbow twinge, you know that sprains, strains, swelling, and soreness can slow life down—fast. Luckily, there Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
If you’ve ever dealt with a twisted ankle, sore knee, or that all-too-familiar tennis elbow twinge, you know that sprains, strains, swelling, and soreness can slow life down—fast.

Luckily, there are some tried-and-true recovery tools that can help you bounce back and feel like yourself again. But not all products are created equal. Some offer quick relief, others provide longer term support—and the best combine both.

Here are the 5 recovery items to keep in your self-care toolkit—plus why 3M FUTURO™ Brand Premium Compression Sleeves just might be the game-changer you’ve been looking for.

1. FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves 

Best for: Compression & support for weak, injured or sore knee, ankle or elbow

When it comes to muscle and joint pain stiffness, soreness, and swelling, compression is key—but comfort is non-negotiable. That’s where FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves shine. Designed by a team of engineers and medical professionals, these sleeves deliver moderate to firm compression that moves and stretches with you.

✅ Breathable, ultra-soft knit

✅ Four-way stretch for natural movement

✅ Stays in place with no-slip silicone

✅ No cutouts = no chafing rubbing

✅ Targeted support options like side knee stabilizers and wrap-around elbow strap

Other sleeves and braces can slide down, feel too tight, or make everyday movement awkward. FUTURO™ Brand helps to solve those problems—making it great for those recovering from a sprain or dealing with stiffness or soreness.

Explore FUTURO™ Compression Sleeves and read more about how compression works. 

2. Cold Packs

Best for: Reducing immediate swelling and numbing acute pain

Ice is a classic for a reason—cold therapy helps minimize swelling and reduce pain in the first 24–48 hours after an injury. Keep a reusable cold pack in the freezer for easy access when you need it.

✅ Great for early-stage injuries

✅ Easy to use

❌ Doesn’t offer ongoing support

❌ Limited use once swelling subsides

3. Topical Pain Relief Creams

Best for: Temporary muscle pain and stiffness relief

Pain relief creams like menthol gels or arnica balms can ease discomfort in sore or overworked muscles. They’re especially helpful for minor aches and stiffness.

✅ Fast-acting pain relief

✅ Easy to apply on the go

❌ Short-lasting effects

❌ No structural support or healing boost

While these are great, they’re not a replacement for physical support like compression gear.

4. Traditional Hinged or Hard Braces

Best for: Post-injury recovery or instability

Hard braces or hinged supports are sometimes necessary for more serious injuries or recovery. They provide rigid stabilization but tend to be bulky, uncomfortable, and hard to wear long-term.

✅ Maximum joint restriction

✅ Doctor-recommended for major injuries

❌ Heavy, sweaty, and hard to wear under clothes

❌ Bulky, uncomfortable and restrictive to movement

Unless your injury is severe, most people prefer a compression option like FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves that offers flexible support while keeping you mobile. To explore other options, visit FUTURO™ Brand to see the full line of products.  

5. Foam Rollers & Massage Balls

Best for: Muscle recovery, breaking up tightness, improving flexibility

Foam rollers and massage tools are perfect for easing post-workout soreness and promoting circulation. They’re great for stiffness and long-term recovery maintenance.

✅ Helps prevent tightness and stiffness

✅ Increases blood flow

❌ Not ideal for acute injuries

❌ Can be painful if used incorrectly

Final Thoughts: The Best Recovery Tool Is the One You’ll Actually Use

title: Dirk Nowitzki to Headline the Celebrity Pickleball Showdown benefiting the Dirk Nowitzki Foundation at the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships in Dallas
dek: The Celebrity Pickleball Showdown returns to the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships, headlined by Dallas Mavericks legend and NBA Hall of Famer Dirk Nowitzki. The marquee event will take place Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
The Celebrity Pickleball Showdown returns to the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships, headlined by Dallas Mavericks legend and NBA Hall of Famer Dirk Nowitzki. The marquee event will take place on Championship Court at Brookhaven Country Club at 7pm CT on Wednesday, November 5, and will benefit the Dirk Nowitzki Foundation through donations and an on-site raffle. Fans around the country can also catch the action live on Tennis Channel.

Inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2023, Nowitzki played 21 seasons with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks and won an NBA title in 2011. Nowitzki is the only player in NBA history to play for a single franchise for 21 years. A 14-time All-Star, the power forward was named NBA MVP in 2007.

“I have participated in the last few Pickleball Showdowns, and it is always so much fun,” said Nowitzki. “The event gets better every year as the national audience for pickleball continues to grow. We are also extremely grateful for the support the PPA is showing our Foundation this year through the raffle proceeds and encourage everyone to come out and purchase tickets to win some really great items.”

“The Celebrity Pickleball Showdown was a legendary highlight of the 2024 event, with the grandstands rocking and the energy of the fans being on another level,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder and CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “Dirk Nowitzki is a Dallas sports legend, and we couldn’t be more thrilled to have him return to the Celebrity Pickleball Showdown in partnership with the Dirk Nowitzki Foundation!”

The Dirk Nowitzki Foundation is dedicated to putting children first and assisting them through programs focusing on their well-being, health and education. The Dirk Nowitzki Foundation awards grants annually and funds projects to nonprofit organizations which run true to the overall mission of the Dirk Nowitzki Foundation. The Foundation lifts up children who are affected by illness, poverty, abuse and neglect through proper channels of guidance and directs them on a path to success.

This year’s event promises to be yet another great pickleball exhibition. More participants are yet to be announced and will surely provide fans with more great memories to be enjoyed for a lifetime.

Thousands of amateur and professional players are expected to compete at the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships on 80-plus courts, and tens of thousands more fans and attendees are expected to take in the pickleball action and enjoy the festivities on Pickleball Boulevard at Brookhaven Country Club.Individual tickets for the Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships, along with week-long passes, and tickets for pickleball clinics and special events on-site at Brookhaven are available now. Click here for purchase information.

title: STORYLINES FOR THE RATE VEGAS CUP PRESENTED BY HOLLAND AMERICA
dek: OVERALL TOP 5: VENUE/TOURNEY/TV: WOMEN’S SINGLES: MEN’S SINGLES: MIXED DOUBLES: WOMEN’S DOUBLES: MEN’S DOUBLES:
author: Dave Fleming
bodyHtml:
OVERALL TOP 5: 

  • STRATOSPHERE: Anna Leigh Waters has now earned 3 dozen triple crowns, extending her seemingly untouchable record – does she get number 37 in Vegas?
  • NO SPHERE OF INFLUENCE: Men’s singles has produced 7 different winners in the past 8, who will have lady luck on their side and take this title? 
  • PAR(R)IS: Todd hopes to leave Vegas with some gold.  
  • ENCORE: Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio go for their 6th win in a row as a team.
  • GRAND & A HALF: 1,500 points going to the winners of this Cup.  

VENUE/TOURNEY/TV:

  • Tourney #17 on the campaign – return to one of the original spots on the PPA tour at Darling Tennis Center – first time was October of 2020. NOTE: Hayden Patriquin won 4.5 singles that year as a 15-year-old. 
  • Progressive Format: Round of 64 Tuesday, Round of 32 Wednesday, Round of 16 Thursday, Quarterfinal Friday, Semifinal Saturday, and Championship Sunday.  
  • PickleballTV (and the app) will have the coverage, starting each day at 10am Pacific, with Tennis Channel coverage on Saturday & Sunday (10am-1pm Pacific).

WOMEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Kate Fahey, Brooke Buckner, Catherine Parenteau
  • Can anyone stop Anna Leigh Waters (1) who hasn’t lost a singles match in over 500 days? 
  • The newly married Kate Fahey (2) returns as the defending champion.
  • Tough round of 16 potential battle: Catherine Parenteau (7) vs. Genie Bouchard (11) – Parenteau beat Genie in the Bronze match here last year. 
  • Watch out for: Brooke Buckner (6) – had game point in the Finals vs. Waters in Va Beach – but could face Fahey in the quarters. 

MEN’S SINGLES:

  • Defending Medalists: Quang Duong, Connor Garnett, Federico Staksrud
  • Ben Johns is back in singles as the…7 seed.  
  • Hunter Johnson still searching for that elusive win since claiming the top spot in the rankings. 
  • Jack Sock (6) was terrific in Virginia – had match points to reach the Final, will this be his week?
  • Watch out for: Chris Haworth (12) – was brilliant in Virginia Beach in earning his first title as a signed player on the Carvana PPA Tour.

MIXED DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Anna Leigh Waters/Ben Johns, Jorja and JW Johnson, Etta Tuionetoa/Christian Alshon
  • Will the top two seeds Waters/Johns (1) and Johnsons (2) run it back from last week AND last year?
  • Fun new partners alert: Staksrud/A. Truong (7) and Oncins/Parenteau (9).
  • Mixed is so deep – Jade Kawamoto and Hunter Johnson are the 22 seed. 
  • Watch out for: Shock teammates Anna Bright and Hayden Patriquin (3) looking to make a run to the medal stand. 

WOMEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Waters/Parenteau, Rohrabacher/Bright, Jansen/Kovalova
  • They’re baaaack…Bright and Waters (1) were dominant in winning gold in Virginia Beach. 
  • LA Mad Drops MLP teammates Catherine Parenteau and Jade Kawamoto (3) would like another shot at the top seed, having lost 11-1, 11-3 in the Va Beach semis. 
  • First time partners Meghan Dizon and Jackie Kawamoto are a dangerous 5 seed . 
  • Watch out for: Black and Todd (3) – did not get to play the semi-finals in Va Beach due to the injury suffered by Parris in the singles semis – they have golden plans in the desert.  

MEN’S DOUBLES:

  • Defending medalists: Johns/Johns, JW Johnson/Frazier, Staksrud/Wright
  • Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio (1) would play new partners CJ Klinger and Jay Devilliers (5) in the quarters if seeds hold. 
  • Can Matt Wright make another deep run? This week he’s back with Eric Oncins as the 7 seed – earlier this year in the first Vegas event they lost to Patriquin/Staksrud in the bronze match.  
  • Fu Fighters – Ryan Fu/Tyson McGuffin are the 9 seed as new partners. 
  • Watch out for: JW Johnson/Dylan Frazier (4) – back together, won the wooden paddle tourney in Sacramento and look to go 2 for 2 in 2025.

author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
October 12 & 13, 2025.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (2) Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson, 11-7, 11-3, 11-3.

  • Part of Waters’s 36th career Triple Crown and fifth in 2025.

  • On Monday, Johns and Tardio won all six rallies of the suspended Game Three to close out the match.

  • Longest rally: 62 shots.

title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest on the Pickleball Court: Why Every Player Should Be Prepared
dek: It’s a sunny Saturday morning at your local pickleball court. The game is fast-paced, everyone is laughing, and then suddenly, everything stops. A player collapses mid-rally. They’re not moving. They’re Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
It’s a sunny Saturday morning at your local pickleball court. The game is fast-paced, everyone is laughing, and then suddenly, everything stops. A player collapses mid-rally. They’re not moving. They’re not breathing. At that moment, the question becomes: Would you, or anyone else on the court, know what to do?

This scenario is more common than you might think. With pickleball’s rapid rise in popularity, attracting players of all ages, sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) has become one of the most serious medical emergencies the community should be prepared for. 

In recognition of Emergency Preparedness Month, let’s break down what SCA is, how it’s different from a heart attack, and most importantly, the steps pickleball players and facilities can take to save lives.

What Is Sudden Cardiac Arrest?

Sudden cardiac arrest happens when the heart’s electrical system malfunctions. Instead of beating in a steady rhythm, the heart begins to quiver chaotically or stops altogether. Blood flow to the brain and vital organs ceases almost instantly.

When this occurs, the person:

  • Collapses without warning
  • Loses consciousness
  • Stops breathing or is not breathing normally

Without immediate help, SCA is almost always fatal.

Heart Attack vs. Sudden Cardiac Arrest

It’s important to know the difference between these two heart emergencies:

Heart Attack (Plumbing Problem): A blockage in the coronary arteries prevents oxygen-rich blood from reaching part of the heart muscle. The person is often awake, experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath, or nausea. Immediate hospital care is critical.

Sudden Cardiac Arrest (Electrical Problem): The heart’s rhythm stops suddenly, leading to collapse and loss of breathing. Survival depends on immediate bystander action with CPR and an AED.

While a heart attack can sometimes trigger cardiac arrest, the treatments are not the same.

Why Seconds Matter

When someone experiences cardiac arrest, irreversible brain damage can begin within 4-6 minutes. For every minute without CPR and defibrillation, the chance of survival decreases by 7-10%.

On the pickleball court, waiting for an ambulance is not enough. The difference between life and death comes down to bystanders ready to step in.

The Two Lifesaving Tools Every Court Needs

  • CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation)
    • Chest compressions keep blood flowing when the heart has stopped.

  • AED (Automated External Defibrillator)
    • AEDs deliver a controlled shock to reset the heart’s rhythm.
    • They are simple to use; turn them on and follow the voice or visual prompts.
    • AEDs are the only treatment for certain fatal heart rhythms.

Together, CPR and AED use can double or triple survival rates. That’s why preparedness is not optional; it’s essential. 

Steps Every Pickleball Facility and Player Should Take To Be Prepared
  • Locate the AED: Know exactly where the AED is at your courts before starting play.
  • Install an AED if one isn’t available: Courts at rec centers, gyms, and parks should all be equipped. If yours isn’t, advocate for one.
    • AED.US, the official AED provider of the PPA Tour, offers an exclusive Philips OnSite AED Pickleball Bundle that’s perfect for facilities, tournament organizers, and dedicated players who want peace of mind while enjoying the game they love.
  • Create a Court Safety Plan: Assign roles – who calls 911, who begins CPR, who retrieves the AED?
  • Get CPR Certified – Training takes just a few hours.
  • Talk About It With Your League or Club: Awareness and preparation are team efforts.

Pickleball Safety: Play It Safe, Play All Season

Sudden cardiac arrest can’t be predicted, but it can be prepared for. Being prepared transforms a tragedy into a story of survival.

This Emergency Preparedness Month, commit to learning CPR, ensuring AED access at your courts, and talking with fellow players about what to do in an emergency.

Next Steps for Players and Facilities:

  • Find a CPR class through your local Red Cross or American Heart Association, or visit AED.US to find a training class near you.
  • Make sure you or your courts have an AED that is visible, accessible, and maintained. If you need help getting one, visit AED.US for guidance and check out their Philips OnSite AED Pickleball Bundle.
  • Create and practice a court safety plan with your club, league, or facility.

title: The Kawamotos’ Comeback: Behind the Numbers
dek: The Kawamoto sisters won the Veolia Cincinnati Showcase in historic fashion, losing the first two games to Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson then winning the next three. How rare is Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
The Kawamoto sisters won the Veolia Cincinnati Showcase in historic fashion, losing the first two games to Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson then winning the next three.

How rare is what Anna Bright called “a reverse sweep?”

Since the start of 2022, I found only five instances of that happening.

2022: *Nationals, Women’s Doubles: Catherine Parenteau and Anna Leigh Waters def. Anna Bright and Jesse Irvine. (*Not a PPA Tour event that year).

2023: Tournament of Champions (Utah), Men’s Doubles: James Ignatowich and Tyson McGuffin def. A.J. Koller and Riley Newman.

2023: PPA Championships (Las Vegas), Men’s Doubles: Ben Johns and Collin Johns def. Dylan Frazier and J.W. Johnson.

2025: Australia Open, Mixed Doubles: Lacy Schneemann and Tyson McGuffin def. Jesse Irvine and Gabe Tardio.

2025: Cincinnati Showcase, Women’s Doubles: Jackie Kawamoto and Jade Kawamoto def. Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson.

Let’s take a broader look:

When a team is down two-games-to-none in a PPA Doubles Final, how does the match turn out? 

Since the start of 2022, I found 145 matches where a team trailed 2-0.

Lost in three games (swept), 115 times. (79%).

Lost in four games, 22 times. (15%).

Lost in five games, four times (3%). (The Men’s Doubles Final in Mesa this year was one of those matches).

Won in five games, four times (3%).

Yes, the Kawamotos’ victory in Cincinnati was historic and rare, and to do it in a Grand Slam event, for their first career titles, makes it even more special.

title: Championship Sunday Standout Stats from the Veolia Cincinnati Showcase
dek: Mason, Ohio. September 14, 2025. . MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (4) Anna Bright and Andrei Daescu, 11-2, 11-8, 11-9. MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Read more
author: Jim Ramsey
bodyHtml:
Mason, Ohio.

September 14, 2025.

.

MIXED DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters and Ben Johns def. (4) Anna Bright and Andrei Daescu, 11-2, 11-8, 11-9.

  • Waters and Johns: Ninth title this year, and fifth consecutive.
  • Waters and Johns are 53-2 in finals together. (Waters, 55 overall; Johns, 68 overall)
  • Waters and Johns had more Clean Winners, fewer Dinking errors, fewer Serve/Return/Thirds errors.
  • Longest rally: 38 shots.

MEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (1) Ben Johns and Gabe Tardio def. (3) Christian Alshon and Andrei Daescu, 11-2, 11-6, 11-9.

  • Johns and Tardio: Fourth consecutive title.
  • Johns has 52 career Men’s Doubles titles; Tardio has 11.
  • Johns and Tardio had more Clean Winners, 17-9.
  • Daescu: No errors on Serves, Returns, Thirds or Dinks.
  • 14th straight tournament won by a team with at least one player listed at six-feet or taller.
  • Longest rally: 45 shots.

WOMEN’S DOUBLES FINAL: (6) Jackie Kawamoto and Jade Kawamoto def. (4) Tyra Black and Jorja Johnson, 8-11, 7-11, 11-6, 11-8, 11-7.

  • First career titles for both Jackie and Jade Kawamoto.
  • The Kawamotos beat top-seeded Bright and Waters in the semifinals.
  • The Kawamotos are the first team to win a PPA Women’s Doubles Final after trailing two games to none since “at least” the start of the 2022 season. (It happened earlier this year in the Mixed Final in Australia).
  • Longest rally: 59 shots.

MEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (6) Christian Alshon def. (3) Connor Garnett, 11-8, 11-1.

  • Alshon’s third career title, all coming this year.
  • Alshon had more Clean Winners, 14-7.
  • Alshon had fewer Return errors, 5-1.
  • 12th straight tournament won by a player at least six feet tall.
  • Longest rally: 11 shots.

WOMEN’S SINGLES FINAL: (1) Anna Leigh Waters def. (2) Kate Fahey, 11-7, 13-11.

  • Waters has a 53-3 career record in Singles finals.
  • Waters is 42-0 in Finals since losing in June 2022 (Todd Orange County.)
  • Waters has won 15 consecutive tournaments played.
  • Waters had fewer Baseline Drive Errors, 19-6.
  • Fahey had three Game Points in Game Two.
  • Longest rally: 13 shots.

.

For the comprehensive stats of all these gold medal matches, please visit:  facebook.com/groups/propickleballstats

title: PPA Finals Return to San Clemente in May 2026 as Pro Pickleball Calendar Streamlines
dek: The PPA Tour Finals are set to return to Life Time Rancho San Clemente from May 4-10, 2026, as the professional pickleball calendar streamlines. With this shift, the Carvana PPA Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
The PPA Tour Finals are set to return to Life Time Rancho San Clemente from May 4-10, 2026, as the professional pickleball calendar streamlines. With this shift, the Carvana PPA Tour season will culminate in May, at which point the Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) season will begin and run through August.

The PPA Tour Finals are the culmination of all the hard work and competition from the athletes throughout the season. Only the best players from the season will qualify for – and compete in – the PPA Finals, which will put the final stamp onto the 2025-26 PPA Tour season and crown the season’s champions of America’s fastest-growing sport.

“We are thrilled to end our season with the PPA Finals at one of the most spectacular and beloved venues on tour – Life Time Rancho San Clemente,” said Carvana PPA Tour Founder & CEO Connor Pardoe. “This slight restructure of the tour calendar will allow long-standing and brand new fans to better follow both the PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball.”

The remainder of the 2025-2026 PPA Tour season has also been announced, headlined by two Slams – the PPA Masters in Palm Springs and the Veolia Atlanta Pickleball Championships. The spring calendar also welcomes a brand new city for the PPA Tour, as the world’s best players will descend on Nashville in April. Fans can keep up with the events calendars for both the PPA Tour and MLP on their respective websites.

This fresh, dynamic calendar signals a healthy alignment in professional pickleball, with the PPA Tour and MLP providing distinct, enthralling and complete pickleball season formats for fans and enthusiasts across the globe to enjoy.

bodyHtml:
Engineered by Experts. Built for Movement.

When it comes to compression sleeves, comfort and performance shouldn’t be trade-offs. That’s why FUTURO™ Brand has reimagined its line of Compression Sleeves, blending medical expertise with engineering innovation to help keep you moving—comfortably and confidently.

Whether you’re managing joint pain, swelling, or stiffness, recovering from a sprain or strain, or just looking for added support during everyday activities, these sleeves are designed with you in mind. If you’ve struggled with bulky braces, sleeves that slip down, or materials that irritate your skin—this is your upgrade.

The new FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves for the knee, elbow, and ankle offer the support you need with a design you’ll actually want to wear.

What’s New? A Better Fit for Real Life.

These sleeves are more than a visual upgrade. They feature:

  • Ultra-soft, four-way stretch fabric that moves with you
  • A smooth, low-profile construction with no cutouts—helping minimize irritation, chafing, and rubbing
  • A sleek, modern look for use with sports and everyday activities
  • An innovative comfort band with silicone beading to help reduce slipping and rolling throughout the day

Created for people dealing with sore joints, muscle fatigue, swelling, or injury recovery, this collection was co-developed by 3M engineers and a panel of medical professionals, combining real-world insight with technical innovation.

Why Choose Compression Sleeves Over Traditional Braces?

We asked 3M’s Application Engineer, Tanya Beckwith, to break down what makes this new line special:

Q: What makes compression sleeves preferable to traditional braces?

A: Compression sleeves are easier to put on, they are breathable, lightweight and are often more cost-effective than more complex, traditional braces.

Q: What makes this line of compression sleeves comfortable?

A: They are made with our softest elastic knit material that stretches in all 4 directions while also being breathable and moisture-wicking. In addition, we removed the cut out design, which helps reduce chafing and rubbing.

Q: What level of compression and support do the compression sleeves have?

A: These compression sleeves provide moderate to firm levels of compression. The knee sleeve has dual side stabilizers that are removable for adaptable support, and the elbow sleeve has a wrap-around strap for targeted, adjustable compression.

Support You Can Count On.

Whether you’re managing a recent injury, rehabbing a strain, or navigating joint pain, FUTURO™ Premium Compression Sleeves are designed to provide compression:

  • Help relieve muscle and joint swelling, soreness, and stiffness
  • Provides compression and support for weak, injured, or sore knee, ankle and elbow joints
  • Deliver comfortable compression all day long—whether you’re at work, working out, or winding down

So whether you’re powering through your day or prioritizing your recovery, FUTURO™ Brand has your back (and your joints).

Let’s Move.

🔗 Learn more and find your fit at futuro-usa.com/compression.

About Tanya Beckwith

Beckwith is a 3M Application Engineer with 3M specializing in product development, commercialization, and project management across diverse healthcare and consumer sectors. Throughout her career, Beckwith has successfully developed, patented, and brought to market innovative health support products for 3M. In her current role, she plays a pivotal role in enhancing the global business by translating the science behind our products into tangible solutions and enriching the customer experience. Beckwith holds a Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering from the University of Minnesota and a Master of Business Administration from the University of St. Thomas.

title: An Homage to Pickleball: Carvana PPA Tour to Hold Vintage Wooden Paddle Tournament to Commemorate the Founding of the Game
dek: In a celebration of pickleball’s 60th anniversary, the Carvana PPA Tour is thrilled to announce the Pickleball Central Vintage Wooden Paddle Open tournament this September 16-21 in Sacramento, California, at Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
In a celebration of pickleball’s 60th anniversary, the Carvana PPA Tour is thrilled to announce the Pickleball Central Vintage Wooden Paddle Open tournament this September 16-21 in Sacramento, California, at Life Time Arden. In a nod to pickleball’s founding 1965, the Vintage Wooden Paddle Open will be an all-wooden paddle event, meaning all players – including pros and amateurs –  will use traditional wooden paddles, just as the founders of the game used 60 years ago. Upon check-in for the tournament, all players will receive a custom-branded wooden pickleball paddle to play with, similar to the type the founders used in the development of the very first pickleball game.

Player registration for the Pickleball Central Vintage Wooden Paddle Open tournament is currently open. The tournament is expected to draw a sizable crowd of participants and fans alike so it is encouraged to register as soon as possible. For more information, please visit the tournament page here. 

Additionally, top PPA pros will be competing with wooden paddles in singles, doubles and mixed doubles, bringing a great equalizer to the field to see who would have been the best in the world when the sport was founded. The competition is not an exhibition – valuable tour ranking points and prize money are on the line.

The sport of pickleball has come a long way since 1965, having steadily grown throughout the decades since. In recent years, pickleball has exploded in popularity across the United States and globally, with the last three years seeing an more than 300% increase in participation in the U.S., according to the SFIA. In addition to the popularity of recreational play, professional pickleball is becoming big business, with top players earning upwards of $1,000,000 annually and pro female pickleball athletes’ earning more on average than WNBA and NWSL players.

“As the sport of pickleball is currently enjoying a period of enormous success and popularity, it’s important to look back on where we came from and honor the traditions, equipment and style of gameplay that led us to where we are today,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder and CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “The Pickleball Central Vintage Wooden Paddle Open tournament will transport avid pickleball fans and enthusiasts back to 1965, when pickleball first began, but deliver all the community and excitement that the sport brings to players today.”

Life Time Arden will serve as the perfect location to honor pickleball’s past while delivering a superb modern experience. Arden has been keeping Sacramento healthy since 1953 and that legacy is only getting stronger with the opening of Life Time’s newest athletic country and racquet club. With up to 34 pickleball courts and spanning 78,000 square feet across two levels and nestled amongst tree-filled hills, Life Time Arden will treat players to an unmatched venue experience while being set in a historic area.

This tournament promises to be an incredibly rewarding experience for pickleball fans of all ages and skill levels. Whether you are new to the game and wanting to learn more about the history of pickleball, or were there in 1965 for the sport’s infancy, the 2025 Pickleball Central Vintage Wooden Paddle Open is sure to be a rewarding pickleball experience for all.

title: Carvana PPA Tour Announces Groundbreaking Court Streaming Partnership with PlaySight
dek: The Carvana PPA Tour will now stream up to 45 courts at each PPA event, with select matches having live scoring capabilities, including scoreboard overlays, bracket information, and player names, Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
The Carvana PPA Tour will now stream up to 45 courts at each PPA event, with select matches having live scoring capabilities, including scoreboard overlays, bracket information, and player names, as part of a new partnership with PlaySight.  This landmark partnership signifies a breakthrough in how all levels of pickleball are covered, consumed, and experienced by fans across the globe. 

PlaySight, a leader in sports video and broadcast technology, will deploy its cutting-edge GO mobile technology across up to 45 courts at Carvana PPA Tour events and several showcase courts at PPA Challenger Series events. This will result in the live and on-demand streaming of thousands of hours of PPA tournament action, accessible to fans anywhere, anytime, on the PPA Streamed Courts YouTube channel. With this new partnership, the Carvana PPA Tour, and the sport of pickleball, takes a major leap into the future of digital sports broadcasting. 

PlaySight’s platform delivers a full suite of advanced broadcast features, including the capability of live score overlays. This ensures that live court action from the Carvana PPA Tour maintains a professional-grade, television-quality viewing experience, whether on YouTube, or any number of digital destinations. 

“Pickleball is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world, and we’re thrilled to be at the heart of its professional evolution,” said Matt Gibson, Vice President at PlaySight. “This partnership with the Carvana PPA Tour will allow us to deploy our cutting-edge technology at the sport’s premier venues, enhancing the experience for everyone. We’re excited to help power the future of pickleball.”

The partnership reflects the shared commitment between the Carvana PPA Tour and PlaySight to meet the rapidly increasing demand for pickleball content. 

“Our vision has always been to elevate the Carvana PPA Tour to the zenith of pro sports and deliver a world-class experience for fans, players, and partners,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder & CEO of the Carvana PPA Tour. “This new partnership with PlaySight is a huge step forward in how our sport is presented and consumed by fans and players alike. Their state-of-the-art technology makes them the perfect partner as we continue to scale the Carvana PPA Tour and deliver more of the world’s best pickleball to fans and players alike.”

This transformative court-streaming partnership between the Carvana PPA Tour and Playsight will take effect this weekend at the Veolia Bristol Open held at the Bristol Sportsplex in Bristol, TN, from August 6-10, 2025.

title: Emergency preparedness on the pickleball court: Insights from firefighters and pickleball gold medalists
dek: Pickleball is the fastest-growing sport in America. It is bringing together players of all ages for fast-paced, heart-pumping fun. But with its popularity comes a lesser-known reality: cardiac emergencies can Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Pickleball is the fastest-growing sport in America. It is bringing together players of all ages for fast-paced, heart-pumping fun. But with its popularity comes a lesser-known reality: cardiac emergencies can and do happen during play. 

That’s why AED.US and Philips, the official AED provider of the PPA Tour, are partnering to ensure the Philips HeartStart OnSite AED is available courtside at PPA Tour events and facilities across the country. This initiative isn’t just about safety; it’s about saving lives.

To highlight the importance of being prepared, we spoke with Martin and Chris Robertson, firefighter brothers and recent gold medal winners at the 2025 World Police & Fire World Games. Their first-hand knowledge of emergency response offers critical insight for players, spectators, and facilities alike, both on and off the pickleball court.

First things first: What to do if someone collapses

According to Martin, the very first step is simple but critical: “Call 911. That’s the most important thing you can do.”

Once help is on the way, you should check if the person is breathing and has a pulse. If not, start CPR and locate the AED.

“Hopefully they [pickleball facility] have an AED,” Martin adds. “They are very user-friendly. Just pull the pads out, follow the diagrams, and listen to the voice instructions.”

Chris stresses the importance of staying calm: “If you’re going to need help with an AED, just shout for a bystander. Remain calm and follow the instructions. Whoever’s doing chest compressions should keep going until first responders arrive.”

Why AEDs matter, especially in pickleball

Cardiac arrest can happen suddenly, even to healthy and active individuals. And with pickleball’s wide-ranging age groups, being prepared is even more critical.

“Pickleball is super popular,” Chris explains. “There are all different kinds of ages and people playing. A lot of them may disregard health conditions or overestimate their fitness level because the game is so fun.”

Martin puts it simply: “Anytime you’re getting a lot of people together, and then add in an active, cardiovascular sport, having an AED on hand is paramount.”

AEDs save lives, even when you haven’t needed one yet

Martin hasn’t had to use an AED on a call yet, but he knows it’s only a matter of time: “That doesn’t mean it can’t happen, and it most likely will. Having the AED there, plus CPR, is what’s ultimately going to save lives.”

Chris agrees: “An AED can really help the situation. If there’s someone trained, or even just willing to act, it could absolutely be a difference-maker.”

A message to facilities: Don’t wait until it’s too late

When asked what advice they’d give to pickleball clubs or rec centers, the answer was immediate:

“Get one,” says Martin. “You don’t want to be that facility that didn’t have an AED if something happens on your watch.”

Chris echoes the urgency: “Pickleball isn’t just for athletes. It’s for everyone, and that means all kinds of health conditions on the court. The risk is real.”

Be a first responder, on and off the court

You don’t need to be a firefighter to help save a life. A CPR training course and the presence of an AED can empower anyone to make a difference.

“Take a CPR class,” Martin says. “You never know when you’ll need it. It could save a life on a regular afternoon while you’re out having lunch with your kids.”

Chris sums it up perfectly: “Be a first responder, on and off the court, at all times. Someone’s life could be in your hands.”

Want to protect your pickleball court or facility?

Learn more and explore the Philips Onsite AED Pickleball Bundle, designed specifically for pickleball facilities, through the AED.US, Philips, and PPA Tour partnership.

title: LT Pro 48 Pickleball Named Official Ball of Carvana PPA Tour
dek: The Carvana PPA Tour (PPA Tour) and Life Time (NYSE: LTH), the nation’s premier healthy lifestyle brand and a leading provider of pickleball courts in North America, today announced the Read more
author: Nathan Boschult
bodyHtml:
The Carvana PPA Tour (PPA Tour) and Life Time (NYSE: LTH), the nation’s premier healthy lifestyle brand and a leading provider of pickleball courts in North America, today announced the LT Pro 48 Pickleball will become the exclusive ball of the Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) and all of its tournaments and events. Designed by Life Time Founder, Chairman and CEO, Bahram Akradi, and his engineering team, the ball will first be used during the PPA tournament in Bristol, Tenn. in early August. The news comes as Life Time expands its relationship with the PPA to host more tournaments across Life Time’s athletic country clubs. 

The LT Pro 48 Pickleball addresses common frustrations with existing pickleballs with the goals of consistent bounce and durability by featuring holes that are symmetrically spaced, along with chamfered edges to reduce cracking and improve flight.

“Pickleball is more than a sport – it’s a global movement that has brought together people of all abilities, ages and backgrounds,” said Akradi. “Since 2021, we’ve committed to elevating and growing this sport and, with the LT Pro 48, we identified a problem and addressed it by engineering a ball that bounces truer and lasts longer, holding up under the stress of professional play.”

“The LT Pro 48 has been used at two previous PPA Tour events and has received great feedback from both our professional players and amateurs,” said Connor Pardoe, Founder and CEO of the PPA Tour. “With the ever-changing standards in pickleball equipment, the LT Pro 48 has really elevated the quality of what a pro-level ball can be, so we are thrilled our relationship with Life Time allows us to utilize this ball at the highest levels of competition.”

Life Time has quickly expanded its pickleball offerings, establishing itself as the leader in premier pickleball experiences across its athletic country clubs. In the first six months of 2025, 3.1 million participants have taken part in pickleball across the company’s 800+ courts. Life Time members are playing an average of 6.8 times per month in 2025 compared to 3.8 times a month in 2023. Life Time has also delivered 26,000 pickleball lessons across its courts in the first half of 2025.

Earlier this month, Life Time announced its pickleball tournament, the LT Open, with the goal of expanding competitive singles play and increasing the top-tier events it hosts at its locations across North America.

Life Time has long been a key venue for the PPA hosting tournaments at iconic locations such as Peachtree Corners, Georgia, and Rancho San Clemente, California. The appointment of tennis legend Andre Agassi as the inaugural chair of the Life Time Pickleball and Tennis Board further underscores the company’s dedication to expanding access, enhancing programming and building vibrant communities around pickleball.

The LT Pro 48 pickleball is available for pre-order now on PickleballCentral.com and will ship to purchasers and be available in Pickleball Central stores by September 15th. 

To learn more about Life Time Pickleball and find available courts near you, please visit the Life Time location page. You can also follow Life Time Pickleball on Instagram.

For more information about Life Time, visit www.lifetime.life or follow on social media at Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn.

author: Jeff Watson
bodyHtml:
The Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball presented by DoorDash (MLP) are excited to announce Jenius Bank™ – the digital banking division of SMBC MANUBANK, a member of the SMBC Group –  has joined as an official partner for the Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball presented by DoorDash (MLP) throughout the balance of 2025.  Jenius Bank will also serve as the title sponsor of the Pickleball World Championships in Dallas, November 3-9 – the biggest weeklong festival in all of pickleball, America’s fastest growing sport.

At the Pickleball World Championships in 2024, more than 57,500 attendees enjoyed daily festivities on the festival hub of Pickleball Boulevard, including exciting amateur pickleball tournaments and programming, diverse food and beverage options, and shopping – all while witnessing the world’s highest level of pickleball competition in the pro divisions. When all was said and done, the event accounted for $15.7 million in local economic impact, according to an economic impact study by the city of Farmers Branch.

As a leading digital bank, Jenius Bank is on a mission to create a monumental shift in the banking industry by empowering digital-first customers to make smarter financial decisions by providing easy to use tools that take the guess work and hassle out of banking.

“It’s an exciting time for pickleball, and we’re thrilled to partner with Major League Pickleball, the PPA Tour and the Pickleball World Championships alongside SMBC MANUBANK to take these events on the road as we stay true to our commitment to drive innovative solutions for all things consumers crave – whether that’s more seamless banking experiences or playing their favorite sport,” said John Rosenfeld, President of Jenius Bank. “We’re looking forward to showing up for Pickleball fans this season and helping them live richer lives on and off the court.”

Jenius Bank will have a large presence at the remaining 2025 PPA Tour tournaments, MLP events and the World Championships, with unique giveaways and experiences for fans.

“Partnering with Jenius Bank marks a major milestone for our sport, reflecting not only the rapid growth and mainstream momentum of professional pickleball, but also the increasing interest from forward-thinking, national brands that recognize the power and potential of our community,” said Connor Pardoe, CEO of the PPA Tour and MLP. “This partnership is a testament to how far pickleball has come and where it’s headed as we continue to elevate the game alongside the biggest sports in America.”

Tickets for the 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships are currently on sale. Attendees have the option to purchase at the VIP level, Courtside+ and Courtside for the entire week or selected days. Each level features different amenities and viewing options that are curated for every fan’s best viewing experience. More information regarding what fans receive at each level can be found here.

Additionally, the professional players’ schedule for the 2025 Jenius Bank Pickleball World Championships has been announced and will run as follows: 

  • Monday, Nov. 3: Pro Qualifiers, all brackets
  • Tuesday, Nov. 4: Round of 64
  • Wednesday, Nov. 5: Round of 32
  • Thursday, Nov. 6: Rounds of 16
  • Friday, Nov. 7: Quarterfinals
  • Saturday, Nov. 8: Semifinals
  • Sunday, Nov. 9: Carvana Championship Sunday

The official partnership between Jenius Bank and the Carvana PPA Tour and Major League Pickleball (MLP presented by DoorDash) benchmarks the growth and health of professional pickleball and pickleball’s largest event and contributes to the elevation of pickleball alongside other major American sports in terms of celebrated corporate partnerships.

dek: Is your body feeling exhausted and heavy midway through your afternoon pickleball session? Do you find yourself losing focus towards the end of your rec games? Nutrition is often the Read more
author: Emma Santerre
bodyHtml:
Is your body feeling exhausted and heavy midway through your afternoon pickleball session?

Do you find yourself losing focus towards the end of your rec games? 

Nutrition is often the missing link in peak pickleball performance. Whether you’re hitting the court for a casual game or a tournament, fueling your body properly makes all the difference. Start with protein—essential for muscle repair and recovery. Aim for 20-30 grams within an hour after playing to reduce soreness and rebuild muscle. Adequate protein intake helps muscle recovery by 50%.

“Consuming a source of high-quality protein within 30-60 minutes after playing pickleball can help kickstart the recovery process,” according to paddle manufacturer, SCS Pickleball. “Good post-game protein sources include lean meats, fish, eggs, dairy products, and plant-based options like tofu and legumes. Whey protein powder is also a convenient and easily digestible option for post-game recovery.”

When it comes to muscle health, look for supplements backed by real science. Mitopure from Timeline is powered by Urolithin A, a breakthrough postbiotic nutrient that recharges your cells — helping you maintain strength and energy as you age. Strength is essential at any age. Click here to grab your free Mitopure Gummies from Timeline, Official Longevity Partner of the PPA.


Carbs are your quick fuel source—consider a small, carb-rich snack before you hit the court. Think banana with peanut butter or a whole-grain energy bar. Consistent fueling ensures you’re not just playing hard, but playing smart.

“Your body needs carbohydrates before you start playing pickleball. Carbs fuel your muscles and give you energy. Even your brain needs carbohydrates when you’re playing pickleball to help you stay sharp,” according to paddle manufacturer, Paddletek. “Avoid fatty foods because they can weigh you down. Stick with light, carbohydrate-rich snacks. To make sure you don’t have an upset stomach while playing, aim to eat your pre-match meal or snack 3-4 hours before playing… If you only have 30 minutes before playing, skip the peanut butter or hummus and have a handful of crackers to get some carbs into your body.”

Don’t forget about hydration. Dehydration can drop your performance by up to 20%. Drink plenty of water before, during, and after your match to stay sharp and agile. Adding electrolytes can also help maintain energy levels during intense games.

“You should listen to your body and predominantly drink to thirst. This is the mechanism your body has evolved to tell you what it needs. Don’t wait until it is too late as it’s not always clear how long a match will last,” explained Greg Thew, a Precision Fuel & Hydration Customer Service Specialist. “With the limited opportunities that are presented to you in order to rehydrate, it’s important that you take advantage of those moments to replenish your fluid and electrolytes. Utilize the change of ends and breaks in play [during a pickleball match] where drinking may be possible to ensure adequate replacement.”

Don’t wait – start fueling yourself with the nutrients your body needs to be your best self on the court and watch your pickleball game level up.

title: Rallying Against Asthma: Emily’s Story
dek: Sponsored Content This article includes the personal experiences of Emily G, an actual patient with asthma. Individual experiences may vary. This year’s CIBC Texas Open welcomed an Official PPA Partner, Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Sponsored Content

This article includes the personal experiences of Emily G, an actual patient with asthma. Individual experiences may vary.

This year’s CIBC Texas Open welcomed an Official PPA Partner, FASENRA® (benralizumab) injection, for subcutaneous use, to provide education and show support for health both on and off the pickleball court.

FASENRA is a prescription medicine used with other asthma medicines for the maintenance treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma in people 6 years and older whose asthma is not controlled with their current asthma medicines. FASENRA is not used to treat sudden breathing problems. Do not use FASENRA if you are allergic to benralizumab or any of the ingredients in FASENRA. Do not use to treat sudden breathing problems. Please see the full Important Safety Information below, and the Prescribing Information including Patient Information for FASENRA.

Through its partnership with the PPA, FASENRA is championing education and awareness of eosinophilic asthma—a chronic condition that impacts over 80% of adults with severe asthma.1* As part of this multi-year collaboration, FASENRA and the PPA are rallying communities together, encouraging people to talk to their healthcare providers about asthma control and exploring treatments that may help them return to the activities they love—like the fast-growing sport of pickleball.

*A registry study considered ~84% of severe asthma patients most likely to have eosinophilic asthma based on several factors, including increased blood eosinophil levels (≥150 cells/μL).

The partnership brings interactive experiences to life, from digital education to high-energy activations at tournaments across the country. At the CIBC Texas Open in Dallas, fans had the chance to “rally against asthma” at an immersive gameplay experience that combined movement with learning. Players practiced their serve on a ten-feet-tall LED screen by aiming pickleballs on trainers at moving targets representing eosinophils. FASENRA reduces blood eosinophils, a type of white blood cell that may contribute to severe asthma. The mechanism of action in asthma has not been definitively established. Every successful hit earned points, tracked in real-time on a leaderboard.

In addition to the gameplay, attendees could visit the FASENRA booth to learn more about the brand, hear real patient stories, and be better equipped to speak to their doctors about their asthma management plan.

In the spirit of joining together eosinophilic asthma and FASENRA education, we’ve partnered with FASENRA to interview Emily G, a real patient living with severe eosinophilic asthma, who recently shared her journey and her newfound love of pickleball in a brief Q&A.

Could you please share about how your diagnosis originally impacted your active lifestyle? What first got you thinking about wanting to play pickleball?

“I played tennis for about 7-8 years, and I also played a few pickleball games, which I thought were really fun and a different experience compared to tennis. But due to my asthma, I had to use a (rescue) inhaler at times before, while and after I played. It was getting to the point where I thought I could not keep up, so I stopped. 

But my husband wanted to join a pickleball team because pickleball has gotten big in my hometown in Michigan. My husband is an active player now and he keeps saying to me, ‘you know, your asthma is under control.’ So, I don’t really have any excuses! But back then, asthma did take me away from my love of fitness and having an active lifestyle.”

FASENRA is a prescription medicine used with other asthma medicines for the maintenance treatment of asthma in people 6 years and older whose asthma is not controlled with their current asthma medicines. FASENRA helps prevent severe asthma attacks (exacerbations) and may improve your breathing. FASENRA is not used to treat sudden breathing problems. Please continue reading for additional Important Safety Information and see the full Prescribing Information including Patient Information. Always talk to your doctor.

This is Emily’s experience. Individual experiences may vary.

Can you tell us more about your asthma journey and how it led to an eosinophilic asthma diagnosis?

“I also love walking, and I try to take a walk every day. There was a time when I would walk with my husband, and it was difficult to talk and walk at the same time because I could not get enough air. I was in a vicious cycle where I was getting asthma attacks (exacerbations) more often than before. Asthma took me away from everything I loved and everything that I wanted to do.

In late 2021, I was running through the Salt Lake City airport to try to get a flight to see my grandchildren, but I struggled. That’s how bad my symptoms had gotten. So that’s when I decided to take action and have a discussion with my doctor.

It was not until I got a blood test at my doctor’s office where I found out my eosinophil count was high. This eventually led to my diagnosis with eosinophilic asthma.  I discussed the benefits and risks with my doctor and we then added FASENRA to my treatment plan, which has worked for me. 

I now go walking with my daughter, Lizzy, for 2 miles and I feel like I can keep going and going! And I can also keep up and play with my grandkids—who I adore dearly!”

This is Emily’s experience. Individual results may vary.

Please see Important Safety Information below and see the full Prescribing Information including the Patient Information for FASENRA and talk to your doctor.

Do you have any tips or advice for those living with asthma?

“Make sure to seek out doctors or healthcare providers who are up-to-date on treatment options. If recommended, seek a blood test counting eosinophil levels. And lastly, do not give up!”

This is Emily’s experience. Individual experiences may vary.

What do you think about FASENRA’s partnership with the PPA?

“When I first heard about the FASENRA and PPA partnership, I thought it was a great idea! It’s so important to keep educated on health and especially eosinophilic asthma for all patients out there. I think this is a sign from the universe for me to get more into pickleball.”

When do you plan to hit the pickleball courts next?

“I cannot wait to get back to the pickleball courts with my husband and some friends very soon! I might even bring along my grandkids.” 

Visit www.fasenra.com for more information. To find out if FASENRA may be right for you, talk to your doctor. FASENRA will continue their tournament presence this year at the FASENRA Virginia Beach Pickleball Cup (October 8-12), bringing interactive experiences and information. You don’t want to miss it! 

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION 

Do not use FASENRA if you are allergic to benralizumab or any of the ingredients in FASENRA. Do not use to treat sudden breathing problems.

FASENRA may cause serious side effects, including:

  • allergic (hypersensitivity) reactions, including anaphylaxis. Serious allergic reactions can happen after you get your FASENRA injection. Allergic reactions can sometimes happen hours or days after you get your injection. Tell your healthcare provider or get emergency help right away if you have any of the following symptoms of an allergic reaction:
    • swelling of your face, mouth and tongue
    • breathing problems
    • fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)
    • rash
    • hives

Before using FASENRA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • are taking oral or inhaled corticosteroid medicines. Do not stop taking your corticosteroid medicines unless instructed by your healthcare provider. This may cause other symptoms that were controlled by the corticosteroid medicine to come back
  • have a parasitic (helminth) infection
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if FASENRA will harm your unborn baby. Tell your healthcare provider if you become pregnant during your treatment with FASENRA
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if FASENRA passes into your breast milk. Talk to your healthcare provider about the best way to feed your baby if you use FASENRA 
  • are taking prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements

Do not stop taking your other asthma medicines unless instructed to do so by your healthcare provider. Tell your healthcare provider if your asthma does not get better or if it gets worse after you start treatment with FASENRA.

The most common side effects of FASENRA include: headache and sore throat. These are not all the possible side effects of FASENRA.  

Approved Use

FASENRA is a prescription medicine used with other asthma medicines for the maintenance treatment of asthma in people 6 years and older whose asthma is not controlled with their current asthma medicines. FASENRA is not used to treat sudden breathing problems.

Please see full Prescribing Information, including Patient Information and Instructions for Use, and talk to your doctor. 

You may report side effects related to AstraZeneca products (Opens new window).

REFERENCE
1. Heaney LG, Perez de Llano L, Al-Ahmad M, et al. Eosinophilic and noneosinophilic asthma: an expert consensus framework to characterize phenotypes in a global real-life severe asthma cohort. Chest. 2021;160(3):814-830.

US-97095 Last Updated 5/2025

author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Want to play pickleball well into your golden years and maintain your health off the court too? Start strength training. Building muscle isn’t just about looking fit—it’s about keeping your body resilient, healthy and injury-free.

Read on to learn:

  • What sports science knows about the role of muscle in longevity and athletic fitness
  • The new supplement that supports muscle and longevity: Mitopure
  • Essential tips from performance coaches you can use right away
  • Exercises that work for people of all skill levels and experience 

It’s easier than you think to get started, at any age. Strong legs and a stable core help you move faster on the court, pivot with ease, and maintain balance during those tough rallies that demand a little extra to come out on top.

“Due to the size of the court and speed and style of play, pickleball players require a lot of functional flexibility and strength throughout those ranges of motion,” said Joel Watts, personal training leader at Life Time in Charlotte, NC. “Developing strength should be a focus of players’ off-court efforts in order to prevent injury and maximize performance.”

Research shows that maintaining muscle mass as you age can reduce your risk of injury by up to 60%. The body requires the right support to keep doing the things you love. So when it comes to muscle health, look for supplements backed by real science. Mitopure® from Timeline is shown to help you maintain muscle strength and energy as you age.  Learn more and claim a special offer for pickleball players.

Strength is essential for pickleball players who want to stay competitive and agile from the first serve to the final point. Plus, it helps preserve bone density and joint health, reducing the risk of fractures and wear-and-tear injuries that could shut you down for extended periods of time. It’s an investment in your body that pays off with every match. Incorporate strength training into your exercise routine two to three times a week — complemented by specific pickleball exercises and cardiovascular workouts — and you’ll see the difference not just in your game,  but in your daily life, too.

“Strength training is an essential component of any serious pickleball player’s regimen. By focusing on exercises that build upper body strength, core stability, and lower body power, you’ll be well on your way to dominating the court,” said Dr. Erik Korem, a renowned sports scientist and performance coach with the NFL’s New York Jets. “Remember, consistency is key, and integrating these strength training tips into your routine will unlock significant improvements in your game. Embrace the journey and enjoy the rewards of a stronger, more agile, and resilient body.”

Ready to stay strong, sharp, and on your game? Explore the science of Mitopure and give your body the edge it needs—on and off the court.

If you’re looking for inspiration to get your strength training journey started, check out some of these exercises:

Upper body

1. Push-Ups – chest, triceps, shoulders

2. Pull-Ups / Assisted Pull-Ups – back, biceps

3. Dumbbell Shoulder Press – shoulders, triceps

4. Dumbbell Rows or Barbell Rows – upper back, lats, biceps

5. Chest Press (Bench or Dumbbell) – chest, triceps

Lower body

1. Squats (Bodyweight or Weighted) – quads, glutes, hamstrings

2. Deadlifts (Traditional or Romanian) – hamstrings, glutes, lower back

3. Lunges (Walking or Stationary) – quads, glutes, calves

4. Glute Bridges or Hip Thrusts – glutes, hamstrings

Core

1. Planks (Front and Side) – total core

2. Russian Twists – obliques

3. Hanging Leg Raises or Lying Leg Lifts – lower abs

4. Ab Wheel Rollouts – advanced core strength

When doing strength training, keep these tips in mind:

1. Focus on form first and prioritize quality over quantity. Use mirrors or record yourself to check your posture.

2. Start with bodyweight or light weights. This is especially important for beginners to avoid injury.

3. Use “progressive overload” by gradually increasing weight, reps, or intensity to keep building strength.

4. Rest and recovery is important because muscles grow during rest. Allow 48 hours between working the same muscle group.

5. Don’t forget to warm up and cool down, including using a dynamic warm-up (e.g., arm circles, light jogging) and a simple cool down with static stretching to increase flexibility and reduce soreness.

6. Balance push and pull movements to avoid muscle imbalances by training both anterior and posterior chains.

7. Stay consistent — 2–4 strength sessions per week is great for most people.

8. Track your progress by using a journal or app to monitor weights, reps, and improvements.

9. Eat well to build strength with an emphasis on protein (1.2–2.0g/kg of bodyweight), complex carbs, and healthy fats.

10. Breathe properly by timing your exhale during exertion (lifting) and your inhale during release.

title: Healthy Tips to Keep You on the Pickleball Court
dek: Healthy behaviors and routine cancer screenings can help you stay in the game this spring, and for many seasons to come. Millions of people are diagnosed with cancer each year, Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Healthy behaviors and routine cancer screenings can help you stay in the game this spring, and for many seasons to come.

Millions of people are diagnosed with cancer each year, but with the right lifestyle choices, and adherence to screening guidelines many can significantly reduce their risk. For those who do develop cancer, recommended screenings and regular doctor visits can lead to early detection. When followed up with expert cancer care, early-stage diagnoses often result in better outcomes and quality of life.

Here are some of the ways you can reduce your risk of cancer diagnosis and death, including diet, exercise genetic testing and more.

Exercise

“Exercise plays a crucial role in reducing the risk of several types of cancer,” OSUCCC – James behavioral scientist Roberto Benzo, PhD, says. “Physical activity is linked to lower risk of cancer, including breast, colon, endometrial, kidney, bladder, esophageal, and stomach cancers.

For pickleball players, the cardiovascular benefits of the sport also come with a boost of cancer-prevention perks.

“Cardiovascular exercise improves metabolic function and supports weight management, a key factor in reducing risk, particularly for hormone-related types like breast and endometrial cancers.” Benzo says. “Social engagement in sports like pickleball can improve mental health and reduce stress, which contribute to overall well-being and may indirectly lower cancer risk.”

Nutrition

Our eating habits significantly impact all aspects of health, including cancer risk.

“Think of food as medicine. What we eat should be enjoyable, but we should also eat in a healthy way to reduce the risk of cancer,” says Fred Tabung, PhD, a researcher at The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center – James Cancer Hospital and Solove Research Institute (OSUCCC – James).

Tabung and his colleagues recommend a largely plant-based diet to promote cancer prevention and overall health, though there is room for diverse food choices, including lean meats and other healthy proteins.

“It doesn’t have to be vegan or vegetarian — the goal is to fill the majority of your plate with fruits and vegetables and whole grains,” he says.

Stay safe in the sun

Skin cancer is the most common form of cancer in the U.S., but many of those cases could be prevented by following some simple sun safety tips, like using sunscreen and wearing protective clothing.

“Sun protection is all about reducing UV ray exposure, so it’s important to make sure you’re using sunscreen when outside and reapplying when needed, which can vary depending on the SPF,” OSUCCC – James oncologist Merve Hasanov, MD, says. “Remember that UV rays can also come through clouds, so skin protection is important no matter the weather.”

Know your family history

Not all cancers can be prevented through lifestyle choices, so learning about family health history is an important part of any prevention plan. Equipped with the right knowledge, patients can work with genetic counselors to identify and monitor risk factors, increasing the chances of cancer prevention for themselves and their families.

“When we think of family history in terms of cancer genetics and inherited genetic mutations, we think about a broad spectrum of relatives, more than just your parents and siblings,” says Leigha Senter, MS, CGC, a licensed genetic counselor at the OSUCCC – James. “We ask about grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins, and that can inform us about how likely people are to have hereditary predispositions for cancer.”

Uncovering inherited genetic mutations leads to earlier and more frequent screenings that can detect cancer in its earliest and most treatable stages.

Cancer screenings save lives

Catching cancer at its earliest stages can dramatically increase the chances of survival, so recommended screenings are core components of comprehensive health.

OSUCCC – James experts specialize in screening tests for several types of cancer, including:

Breast cancer: Mammogram tech has improved dramatically over the years, currently utilizing 3D tomography to detect breast cancer at its earliest stages. OSUCCC – James experts recommend annual mammograms for women 40 and over, or earlier depending on risk.

Lung cancer: Tobacco use is the leading cause of lung cancer, so smokers with a histories of smoking one pack a day for 20 years, or ex-smokers who have quit within the past 15 years, should undergo screening, according to OSUCCC – James experts.

Cervical cancer: Annual Pap tests aren’t just great tools for diagnosing cervical cancer, they can also help with prevention by identifying abnormal or precancerous cells around the cervix. Testing is also available for HPV, which can dramatically raise the risk of cervical cancer.

Skin cancer: Dermatologists can screen for melanoma and other cancers by examining patients’ skin for signs of abnormal moles, birthmarks or other pigmented areas. It’s also important for people at home to keep an eye on moles and other skin spots, following the ABCDE method and consulting doctors if they see any of the following red flags:

  • Asymmetry: One half of the spot doesn’t match the other half.
  • Border: The edges of the mole are uneven or ragged.
  • Color: The spot has multiple colors, and the color pattern may be changing.
  • Diameter: The spot is six millimeters — the diameter of a typical pencil eraser—or larger.
  • Evolving: The spot or mole changes in shape, color or size.

title: PPA, AED.US, and Philips Partner to Make Pickleball Safer—One Court at a Time
dek: Safety should always be a top priority in pickleball’s fast-paced, high-energy world. That’s why AED.US, a leading provider of automated external defibrillators (AEDs), and Philips, a focused leader in AED Read more
author: PPA Tour
bodyHtml:
Safety should always be a top priority in pickleball’s fast-paced, high-energy world. That’s why AED.US, a leading provider of automated external defibrillators (AEDs), and Philips, a focused leader in AED manufacturing, are proud to announce their new partnership with the Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) and the PPA Tour.  

Together, they’re raising awareness about sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) and ensuring the lifesaving Philips HeartStart OnSite AED is available wherever pickleball is played—from courts to clubs to home training spaces. Whether you’re a casual player enjoying weekend matches or a competitor battling it out in a tournament, being prepared for the unexpected can mean the difference between life and death.

“At AED.US, we’re proud to partner with Philips and the PPA to bring greater awareness and access to the life-saving Philips HeartStart OnSite AED in the pickleball community,” said Rob Vaka, VP of Strategic Growth (AED.US). “This partnership is about empowering players, coaches, and venues with the tools and confidence to save lives when every second matters.”

Pickleball is booming—with over 35 million players nationwide, many of whom are active older adults. As the sport grows, so does the need for improved safety measures.  

Sudden cardiac arrest remains a public health crisis, with over 1,000 SCA events happening each day in the U.S. For every minute that a victim goes without defibrillation, the chance for survival decreases by 10%. 

Having an easily accessible AED can be the difference between life and death and that’s why AED.US is on a mission: to make AED access as common as pickleball paddles. Through the partnership with the PPA, they are working to educate and equip the pickleball community with the tools and training needed to respond to SCA.

In addition to becoming the official AED provider of the PPA Tour, AED.US and Philips will collaborate on a collection of activations and offers to elevate this important partnership.

Courtside AED Access at all PPA Tour Tournaments

At all future PPA Tournaments in 2025, a Philips HeartStart OnSite AED will be available courtside in case of an emergency, helping protect players, coaches, and spectators alike from SCA. 

The Philips Onsite AED Pickleball Bundle – Only at AED.US

Studies show that racket sports like pickleball can reduce the risk of death by nearly 50% compared to non-players. 9 were defended successfully, continuing the rally. (50%)

ATP DEFENSE RATE 

MEN’S DOUBLES FINALS:

32 ATPs were hit into the opponent’s court.

19 were either “clean winners” or not returned successfully. (60%)

13 were defended successfully, continuing the rally. (40%)
